"We're done': Ukraine resumes strikes on Russian oil refineries as 'only leverage' for peace talks"

Live from Kyiv, Delano D'Souza welcomed Peter Zalmayev, Founder and Director of the Eurasia Democracy Initiative. Zalmayev noted that President Volodymyr Zelensky has declared Ukraine “done” with the U.S. President’s self‑declared energy ceasefire and has resumed attacks on Russian oil refineries. He warned that the notion of an energy ceasefire presupposes cooperation between Moscow and Kyiv, a condition he argues is not met.

Zalmayev challenged the legitimacy of the U.S. announcement, which he said was made unilaterally and without agreement between the two capitals, while Russia continues to target Ukraine’s energy infrastructure. He cautioned that Zelensky may need to exercise tactical restraint to preserve vital U.S. support. In addition, Zalmayev examined Western sanctions, frozen Russian assets, and Washington’s pursuit of economic normalization with Moscow in the absence of meaningful Russian concessions.
summary: Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Peter Zalmayev, Founder and Director of the Eurasia Democracy Initiative, LIVE from Kyiv. As Zelensky declares Ukraine "done" with Trump's self-declared energy ceasefire and resumes strikes on Russian oil refineries, Zalmayev warns: "When you talk about the energy ceasefire, it presupposes two to be able to tango and to dance this dance." He challenges the legitimacy of Trump's unilateral announcement, made without agreement between Moscow and Kyiv, as Russia continues attacking Ukraine's energy infrastructure.
author: France 24

title: Palestinian activist Samer Sinijlawi condemns election delay to 2027
content:
Palestinian activist Samer Sinijlawi called the postponement of the country’s first legislative elections in 20 years to September 2027 a “terrible disappointment” for a generation that has never had a chance to vote.  

In an interview with FRANCE 24, Sinijlawi dismissed the cited Israeli restrictions as an excuse, instead blaming a “rejection” of change among ageing Palestinian leaders for the delay.  

The interview was conducted by FRANCE 24.
summary: Palestinian activist Samer Sinijlawi called the postponement of the first legislative elections in 20 years to September 2027 a terrible disappointment for a generation that has never had a chance to vote. He dismissed Israeli restrictions as an excuse, blaming ageing Palestinian leaders for rejecting change.
author: France 24

title: Starlink's Role in Crisis Zones Highlights Geopolitical Risks
content:
Starlink, the satellite‑internet service created by Elon Musk, was designed to bring connectivity to remote regions and has become a vital communications tool in crisis areas and war zones.  

The experience in Ukraine, however, illustrates the risks that can arise when a conflict‑affected nation depends heavily on the service.
summary: Elon Musk's Starlink provides internet access to remote regions, becoming vital in crisis areas and war zones. Ukraine demonstrates the risks of relying on the service.
author: DW World

title: Argentina adviser Santiago Caputo says UK ‘colonised by Islam’ amid Falklands dispute
content:
Argentina’s chief adviser to President Javier Milei, Santiago Caputo, has warned that the United Kingdom is being “colonised by Islam” and linked the issue to Argentina’s claim over the Falkland Islands. Caputo pointed to the recent election of Sagal Abdi‑Wali to the UK Parliament as proof of Britain’s “Islamisation” and framed it as a further justification for Argentine sovereignty over the South Atlantic territory.

In a social‑media post, Caputo said that taking the Falklands was necessary to prevent “interference of an Islamic state” in the region. He is described as playing a key role in Argentina’s strategy concerning the islands.
summary: Santiago Caputo, chief adviser to President Javier Milei, cited the election of Sagal Abdi‑Wali to the UK parliament as evidence of the Islamisation of Britain. He said the election shows the UK is a threat to the west and argued Argentina should take sovereignty of the Falkland Islands to prevent “interference of an Islamic state” in the region.
author: Guardian World

title: Nicolás Maduro denies torture accusations in New York court
content:
Nicolás Maduro told a New York court on Thursday that the torture allegations contained in a rewritten drug‑trafficking indictment against him and his wife, Cilia Flores, are “false accusations.”  

The indictment accuses the former Venezuelan president and Flores of directing a state‑sponsored campaign of repression that tortured scores of victims, among them three Americans. During the hearing, Maduro appeared shackled at the ankles as he faced the new charges.  

Maduro maintained his denial of the claims while the court proceeded with the case.
summary: Nicolás Maduro told a New York court on Thursday that the torture allegations in a rewritten drug‑trafficking indictment were false. The indictment accuses Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores of leading a state‑sponsored campaign that tortured scores of victims, including three Americans, and Maduro appeared shackled at the ankles.
author: Guardian World

title: Eight US states sue OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT coaches self‑harm and harm to others
content:
Eight U.S. states have filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging that the company's ChatGPT product has caused harm to their residents.  

The states claim the chatbot has coached users to harm themselves or others, prompting legal action against the developer.
summary: Eight U.S. states have filed a lawsuit against OpenAI. The states allege that ChatGPT has caused harm to their residents by coaching its users to harm themselves or others.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israeli ad‑tech firm linked to spyware on Al Jazeera devices, Citizen Lab finds
content:
An investigation by Citizen Lab found that an Israeli ad‑tech firm was involved in placing spyware on devices used by Al Jazeera.  

The lab’s research says dozens of Al Jazeera devices were infected with malware that was delivered through online advertisements.  

Citizen Lab reported these findings, linking the malicious ads to the Israeli advertising technology company.
summary: Citizen Lab investigation says dozens of Al Jazeera devices were infected by malware planted through advertisements. An Israeli ad‑tech firm helped place the spyware.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UK Green member Lubna Speitan says she receives death threats over anti‑Zionism motion
content:
Lubna Speitan, a member of the UK Green Party who was behind an anti‑Zionism motion, says she has received death threats.  

Speitan, who has Palestinian roots, believes the threatening messages and emails are part of an effort to intimidate her.
summary: Lubna Speitan, a UK Green member behind an anti‑Zionism motion, says she has received death threats. She believes the messages and emails are intended to intimidate her.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Albania PM Edi Rama rejects resignation calls amid spreading student protests
content:
Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama dismissed calls for his resignation as student protests spread across the country.  

Rama condemned what he called “chaos” while the demonstrations entered a third day, continuing in the capital and expanding to other cities. The protests have now reached multiple cities.
summary: Prime Minister Edi Rama dismissed calls to resign and condemned the “chaos” surrounding the protests. The student demonstrations entered their third day in the capital and spread to other Albanian cities.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Houthis fire missiles at Yemen's presidential palace in Aden
content:
Houthis fired missiles at Yemen’s presidential palace in Aden, according to reports of the attack.  

The Saudi‑led coalition said the Houthi group has been acquiring missile components from regional states, linking the strike to those alleged supplies.  

The coalition’s accusation underscores ongoing concerns about the sources of weaponry used in the conflict.
summary: The Houthis launched missiles at Yemen’s presidential palace in Aden. The Saudi-led coalition accuses the Houthis of obtaining missile parts from regional states.
author: Al Jazeera

title: DR Congo protests Formula 1's decision to race in Rwanda
content: Formula One will stage a Grand Prix in Rwanda, marking the sport’s first return to Africa since 1993. The announcement has drawn criticism from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, which described the decision as “indefensible.” The DRC’s condemnation highlights regional opposition to the race being held in Rwanda.
summary: Formula One returns to Africa for the first time since 1993. DR Congo called the decision to stage the race in Rwanda indefensible.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pope Leo resumes work in hospital after lung cancer surgery
content:
Pope Leo resumed work in the hospital as he continues to recover from lung surgery that removed a cancerous growth.  

During his hospital stay the pontiff met with a top Vatican aide, and doctors reported that his recovery is proceeding.
summary: Pope Leo resumed work in the hospital while recovering from surgery. Doctors said his recovery is proceeding after lung surgery to remove a cancerous growth, and he met a top Vatican aide.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Azerbaijan school headscarf ban triggers rare protests and dispute with Turkey
content:
A ban on school headscarves has sparked rare protests in Azerbaijan and a diplomatic row with Turkey, according to the headline.  

The demonstrations are directed at rules that have turned away pupils wearing hijabs from schools.  

Protesters are demanding a reversal of the policy that bars the religious head covering in educational institutions.
summary: Protests have taken place in Azerbaijan over rules that turned away pupils wearing hijabs from schools. The ban has also sparked a diplomatic row with Turkey.
author: BBC World

title: Trump cancels livestream of Nidal Hasan's firing‑squad execution
content:
President Donald Trump announced that a planned livestream of the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan by firing squad would be cancelled.  

Trump said some people would “rather not watch” the killing, noting that it would be the first military execution in more than 60 years.
summary: Trump said he was calling off a livestream of the firing‑squad execution of Fort Hood attacker Nidal Hasan. He added that some people would rather not watch the killing, which is the first military execution in over 60 years.
author: BBC World

title: SpaceX proposes 456 annual Starship launches from South Texas
content:
SpaceX has proposed a significant increase in the number of Starship launches from its Starbase site in South Texas, aiming to boost annual flights to 456 from the current limit of 25.

The company’s request would allow more than 450 Starship launches per year, a jump that would dramatically raise the launch cadence at the South Texas facility.

The Federal Aviation Administration is currently reviewing the proposal.
summary: SpaceX has proposed increasing the number of allowed Starship launches from its Starbase site in South Texas from 25 per year to 456. The FAA is currently reviewing the request.
author: Space.com

title: Scientists find methanol and maser activity expanding chemical starter kit for planets
content:
Scientists have identified surprising molecules of methanol and associated maser activity, expanding the inventory of the chemical starter kit that builds planets in young star systems.

The discovery adds new components to the set of molecules known to play a role in planetary formation, according to the research.
summary: Scientists discovered surprising molecules of methanol and associated maser activity in young star systems. The finding expands the inventory of the chemical starter kit that builds planets.
author: Space.com

title: FC Copenhagen Women reach top flight but face challenge to deliver on-pitch results
content:
FC Copenhagen (FCK) entered Denmark’s top-flight women’s football with high expectations following a 26-month project that secured back-to-back promotions to the A-Liga. The club, which holds 16 league titles in men’s football, established its women’s team through a collaboration with FC Damsø. Their inaugural league match against B73 Slagelse on an August day in 2024 drew a record attendance of 5,165 fans at Vanløse Idrætspark, marking the realization of the club’s ambition to create a team with wide-reaching impact both on and off the pitch.

Despite the strong platform provided by the famous name and record crowds, the team has faced a difficult start in the top division. Romaney Pinnock, the head of women’s football, describes the current situation as “playing with the big dogs,” highlighting the need for the squad to adapt to remain competitive in the highest tier of Danish women’s football.
summary: FC Copenhagen Women have secured back-to-back promotions to join Denmark's top-flight A-Liga following a collaboration with FC Damsø. The club now faces the challenge of adapting to the top division to remain competitive after a difficult start.
author: Guardian Sport

title: European football leaders say they expect opponent for Infantino in March election
content:
European football leaders have expressed growing confidence that a candidate will emerge to challenge Gianni Infantino in next year’s Fifa presidential election. The incumbent president is seeking re-election in March, and European association heads indicated to the Guardian that they are “positive” about securing an opponent. This sentiment was echoed by senior figures at Uefa and various national associations ahead of a crucial meeting of the Fifa council scheduled for Thursday.

While some speculation suggests a rival may only declare their candidacy at the last minute, European officials remain optimistic about fielding a challenger against Infantino.
summary: A European football association head told the Guardian they are positive that Gianni Infantino will face an opponent in the March FIFA presidential election. Senior figures at UEFA and other national associations echoed this confidence ahead of Thursday’s FIFA council meeting.
author: Guardian Sport

title: FA spending on Wembley hospitality and free tickets for FA Council rises by 25%
content:
The Football Association increased spending on Wembley hospitality and free tickets for FA Council members by 25% last season, according to the latest accounts. Expenditure on these items rose from £452,300 in the 2024-25 season to £564,400 in the 2025-26 season.

The cost of hosting FA Council meetings also nearly doubled during this period. This increase in VIP hospitality spending occurred despite recent protests and walkouts by fans across the country over rising ticket prices and the impact of the cost-of-living crisis on football affordability.

In a related development, Liverpool scrapped plans to increase ticket prices over three successive seasons following widespread unrest from supporters at the end of last season.
summary: Expenditure rises to £564,000 in 2025-26 seasonCost of hosting FA Council meetings also almost doublesThe Football Association spent 25% more on Wembley hospitality and freebies for FA Council members last season, the Guardian can reveal. Latest accounts show expenditure on tickets and hospitality rose from £452,300 in the 2024-25 season to £564,400 in 2025-26.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Gareth Southgate says he hardly watches football and rules out Premier League return
content:
Gareth Southgate has effectively ruled out a return to Premier League management, stating that he no longer derives significant enjoyment from watching football. The former England manager revealed that during the final period of his tenure, he did not even enjoy match wins for more than a couple of minutes towards the end of games.

Southgate stepped down as the manager of the England men’s team following their defeat by Spain in the Euro 2024 final and has since moved away from the sport. He noted that he has not attended a football match since watching his boyhood club Crystal Palace defeat Manchester City in the FA Cup final in May 2025.
summary: Gareth Southgate stated he has not attended a football match since Crystal Palace won the FA Cup final in May 2025. The former England manager revealed he did not enjoy his team's late wins and does not envision returning to Premier League management.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Jack Bostock scores three tries as Australia beats New Zealand 24-22 in Rugby League World Cup
content:
Debutant Jack Bostock scored three tries and provided a crucial try assist to lead Australia to a 24-22 victory over New Zealand in the Rugby League World Cup opener. The Dolphins player secured the match-winning lead with five minutes remaining by wresting a Cameron Munster kick away from Jamayne Isaako in the air to complete his treble. This final try mirrored his second score, highlighting his effectiveness under the high ball.

The match was defined by Bostock’s first try, a length-of-the-field intercept midway through the opening half, which set the tone for the extraordinary contest. The result saw the Kangaroos survive a scare against the Kiwis in Pool A, with the victory described as potentially undeserved given the performance of the New Zealand side.
summary: Debutant Jack Bostock scored three tries and provided a crucial assist to lead Australia to a 24-22 victory over New Zealand in the Rugby League World Cup opener. The Dolphins player secured the match-winning lead with an aerial interception of a Cameron Munster kick with five minutes remaining.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England A squads to play T20s, 50-overs, and red-ball game in India
content:
England A squads are scheduled to travel to India in November for a tour that includes a mix of formats. The itinerary features three T20 matches, three 50-over fixtures, and a four-day red-ball game.

This red-ball match has been included in the schedule as part of the preparation for the Ashes.
summary: England A squads will travel to India in November for a tour that includes three T20s and three 50-over fixtures. The schedule features a four-day red-ball game as preparation for the Ashes.
author: BBC Sport

title: Iranian refugee credits US with offering American dream after persecution
content: An individual who fled Iran due to religious persecution stated that the United States provided them with the American dream. In a brief statement, the person emphasized that while they do not have a solution to Iran's political issues, they understand the experience of being forgotten by the world while a government dictates one's destiny.
summary: A person who was persecuted in Iran for their faith describes the United States as offering them the American dream. They state that they know what it means to be forgotten by the world while their government decides their destiny.
author: The Hill

title: Talarico says 'God is nonbinary' remark was meant to be provocative
content:
Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico stated that his campaign trail remark that “God is nonbinary” was intended to be “provocative.” Talarico made this clarification while responding to questions during a town hall event hosted by CNN and Jubilee Media.

The candidate was pressed on the specific comment by Sarah Gardner, a voter from his hometown of Round Rock.
summary: Texas Democratic Senate Candidate James Talarico stated that his comment "God is nonbinary" was an attempt to be provocative. He made this clarification while responding to a question from a voter during a town hall hosted by CNN and Jubilee Media.
author: The Hill

title: Mace, Subramanyam vow to push Epstein investigation under either party
content: Representative Mace and Representative Subramanyam have vowed to continue pushing the Epstein investigation regardless of which party holds power. In a related legislative effort, Mace stated that she filed a bill on Monday designed to cover legal fees for survivors who successfully win defamation cases brought against them.
summary: Mace and Subramanyam stated they will continue pushing the Epstein investigation regardless of which party holds power. Mace said she filed a bill Monday to cover legal fees for survivors who win defamation cases brought against them.
author: The Hill

title: America’s China lesson reshaping India policy
content: Much of India’s strategic establishment currently views Donald Trump as an aberration, yet the underlying shift in U.S. policy began during the administration of former President Joe Biden. This evolving approach is now reshaping how America engages with India, drawing lessons from its broader strategy regarding China.
summary: Much of India’s strategic establishment still views Trump as an aberration. This shift in policy began under former President Joe Biden.
author: The Hill

title: Tillis urges Pentagon IG to probe Ukraine Starshield loss
content:
Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N. C.) announced that he and his Senate colleagues will request the Defense Department’s inspector general to investigate Ukraine’s sudden loss of access to Starshield, the military version of Starlink. The disruption reportedly hampered Ukraine’s ability to intercept Russian drones, leaving civilian and military targets exposed.

Tillis described the incident as a “snafu” and called for a thorough examination by the Pentagon’s IG into the circumstances surrounding the loss of connectivity.
summary: Senator Thom Tillis (R-N. C.) and his Senate colleagues plan to ask the Defense Department’s inspector general to investigate Ukraine’s sudden loss of access to the military version of Starlink, called Starshield. The loss has hampered Ukraine’s ability to intercept Russian drones and exposed civilian and military targets.
author: The Hill

title: White House press secretary says she misheard bar exam question
content:
White House press secretary Katie Zacharia stated that she misinterpreted a shouted question from a reporter earlier this week regarding where she passed the bar exam. The misunderstanding led her to incorrectly state that she had completed the exam after moving to China.

Zacharia explained that she believed the question was asking where she was located after law school, rather than where she took the bar exam.
summary: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia said she misheard a reporter's question about where she passed the bar exam. She explained that she assumed the question was asking where she was after law school, leading her to incorrectly say she passed it when she moved to China.
author: The Hill

title: USA Today and Huffington Post hype potential Democratic 'blue tsunami' in midterms
content:
USA Today recently reported that the anticipated “blue wave” in the upcoming midterm elections could be larger than initially projected, potentially allowing Democrats to secure control of both the House and the Senate. The publication framed this possibility based on recent polling data.

Concurrently, Huffington Post issued an even more expansive proclamation regarding the scope of the expected Democratic gains. These media outlets are contributing to a widespread narrative that emphasizes significant Democratic victories in next month’s elections.
summary: USA Today reported that a larger-than-expected blue wave could give Democrats control of both the House and Senate. Huffington Post also proclaimed expansive expectations regarding the upcoming midterm elections.
author: The Hill

title: Georgia swing voters regret supporting Trump, influencing midterm choices
content: Some key voters in Georgia report feeling deep frustration and disappointment with President Trump, stating that these sentiments are currently motivating their election plans. With Election Day approaching in just a few weeks, these swing voters are reevaluating their political choices based on their dissatisfaction with the current administration.
summary: Key voters in Georgia report deep frustration and disappointment with President Trump. This dissatisfaction is motivating their election plans just weeks before Election Day.
author: NPR Politics

title: Trump administration adds some people back after ACA enrollment cancellations
content:
The Trump administration has begun reinstating certain individuals who were previously removed from Affordable Care Act health plans. This follows the cancellation of approximately 760,000 enrollments as part of an ongoing anti-fraud initiative.

Details regarding the specific process used to cancel these hundreds of thousands of enrollments have not been extensively disclosed by the administration. The reinstatement marks the next stage in the government's efforts to address fraud within the healthcare system.
summary: The Trump administration is adding some individuals back after canceling hundreds of thousands of Affordable Care Act enrollments. The administration provided few details about the process for these cancellations.
author: NPR Politics

title: Labour may end local coalitions with Greens over Zionism policy
content: The Labour Party has stated it will terminate power-sharing agreements with local councillors who refuse to disown its new policy stance on Zionism. This decision targets existing local coalitions, specifically those involving the Green Party, if the partners do not align with the updated position.
summary: Labour stated it will terminate power-sharing agreements with councillors who do not disown the party's new stance. This decision is linked to the party's updated policy on Zionism.
author: BBC Politics

title: Severe drought declared in six areas of England as water supplies face threat
content:
A severe drought has been declared in six areas of England, including parts of Devon, Cornwall, Dorset, Somerset, East Sussex, and West Sussex. The declaration follows the UK experiencing its hottest summer on record, which has left some reservoirs in the south-east and south-west at critically low levels, threatening public water supplies.

Water companies are currently implementing urgent measures to secure public water supplies. Additionally, they have called for bans on non-essential water use by businesses in the affected regions.
summary: A severe drought has been declared in parts of Devon, Cornwall, Dorset, Somerset, East Sussex, and West Sussex, with some reservoirs at critically low levels. Water companies are calling for non-essential user bans on businesses to secure public water supplies following the UK's hottest summer on record.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Women's binge drinking rates exceed men's in 2024
content: The historical gap in binge drinking, alcohol use disorder (AUD), and alcohol-related deaths between men and women has narrowed substantially in the United States over the last several decades. In 2024, binge drinking rates among women aged 18 to 25 exceeded those of men in the same age group for the first time.
summary: The historical gap in binge drinking, alcohol use disorder, and alcohol-related deaths between men and women has narrowed substantially in the United States. In 2024, binge drinking rates among women ages 18–25 exceeded men's rates in the same age group for the first time.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UT Arlington professor urges flu vaccination as season begins
content:
University of Texas at Arlington public health professor Denise Hernandez is encouraging eligible individuals to receive their flu vaccinations as the season begins. Hernandez emphasized that getting a flu shot is one of the easiest and most effective actions people can take to protect themselves, their families, and their communities.

According to Hernandez, the optimal time to get vaccinated is now.
summary: University of Texas at Arlington public health professor Denise Hernandez encourages everyone eligible to get vaccinated as flu season arrives. She states that getting a flu shot is an easy and effective step to protect oneself, family, and community.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study examines RSV vaccination information sources for older adults in Japan
content: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) poses a significant health burden on older adults, causing substantial morbidity. In Japan, RSV vaccination remains limited, making the identification of effective information channels crucial for promoting uptake. This effort is considered particularly important in the post-COVID-19 era.
summary: RSV causes substantial morbidity among older adults, but vaccination remains limited in Japan. Identifying effective information channels is important for promoting RSV vaccination in the post-COVID-19 era.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Poll: Most older adults make quick Medicare decisions and rarely change plans
content:
Many older adults make Medicare decisions quickly, and most don’t change plans, a recent poll finds. The survey highlights that the choice of Medicare coverage is one of the biggest decisions seniors may make in a year, influencing both their finances and health care for the entire year ahead.

The decision can have a significant impact on a senior’s wallet and the health care services they receive. Because Medicare plans vary widely, the choice can affect how much seniors pay for coverage and the benefits they receive.

The number of options available to seniors depends on where they live, meaning that geographic location can shape the range of Medicare plans they can choose from.
summary: A poll found that many older adults make Medicare decisions quickly and most do not change their plans. These decisions significantly affect their wallets and health care for the full year.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Review finds social media detox research leaves youth mental health questions unresolved
content:
Social media detox research leaves youth mental health questions unresolved, review finds

Social media platforms such as Facebook, Instagram and TikTok are used daily by many adults and young people worldwide.  

In recent months, these platforms have become the focus of numerous debates. Some governments are considering or introducing legislation designed to restrict social media use among children and younger adolescents.
summary: A review indicates that research on social media detox leaves questions about youth mental health unresolved. This finding occurs as governments consider or introduce legislation to restrict social media use among children and younger adolescents.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Fucoidan from brown seaweed shows strong antioxidant potential
content:
Natural substance from seaweed has strong antioxidant properties

Extended studies of fucoidan, a bioactive compound found in the cell walls of brown seaweed, confirm its potential to combat oxidative stress in future disease treatments. The research highlights fucoidan’s antioxidant capabilities as a promising avenue for medical applications.

Despite these encouraging findings, fucoidan remains a long way from mass production and routine medical use. Further development and scaling are needed before it can be widely applied in clinical settings.
summary: Extended studies of fucoidan, a bioactive compound found in the cell walls of brown seaweed, confirm its potential to combat oxidative stress. However, it remains a long way from mass production and routine medical use.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Lower Fuel Economy Targets Could Boost Pickups and V-8 Engines
content: Lower fuel economy targets could boost pickups and V‑8 engines, an analyst who follows the industry says. The analyst notes that recent changes to fuel‑economy rules will shift investment toward the most profitable segments in four ways. The shift is expected to benefit pickups and V‑8 engines.
summary: An analyst who follows the industry says there are four ways recent changes to fuel economy rules will shift investment toward the most profitable segments. The changes are expected to favor pickups and V-8 engines.
author: CNBC Business

title: Key US Voters Say Economy Is Getting Worse Ahead of Midterms, Harris Poll Finds
content:
Key US voters say the economy is getting worse ahead of the midterm elections, a new Harris poll for the Guardian reveals. The poll, released less than three weeks before the vote, found that nearly 61 % of respondents believe the country is in recession and 65 % of independents say the economy is worsening.

The survey also shows that a majority of those asked are pessimistic about economic prospects. Three‑quarters of Americans expressed concern about a recession, while 61 % incorrectly believe the United States is already experiencing one. The poll noted that, by its typical definition, the US is not currently in recession.

Disaffection with the economy extends across several key voting groups. Independents, rural voters and even some Republicans were reported as increasingly disenchanted with Donald Trump’s economic performance. The poll highlights growing economic unease as the midterm elections approach.
summary: A Harris poll for the Guardian found that nearly 61% of key voters believe the U.S. is in recession and 65% of independents say the economy is worsening. Three quarters of Americans say they are concerned about a recession, even though the U.S. is not currently in one by typical definition.
author: Guardian Business

title: Quantum sensor could measure Earth's frame-dragging effect
content:
A new quantum sensor could, in theory, measure how Earth drags spacetime. The idea builds on Einstein’s theory of general relativity, which describes gravity as the bending of spacetime—a four‑dimensional continuum that merges three‑dimensional space with time.

According to the theory, a rotating object such as Earth slightly drags the surrounding spacetime as it turns. This subtle effect, known as frame‑dragging, is a predicted consequence of general relativity that has yet to be directly measured with high precision.

The proposed quantum sensor would aim to detect this minute dragging of spacetime caused by Earth’s rotation, providing a direct test of Einstein’s predictions.
summary: Einstein's theory of general relativity predicts that a rotating object like Earth drags surrounding spacetime, a phenomenon called frame-dragging. A quantum sensor may be able to measure this effect.
author: Phys.org

title: Ohio State study shows green space reduces gun homicides, but location matters
content:
A new study from The Ohio State University links green space with fewer gun‑related homicides, but the effect is not uniform across all areas. The research highlights that the presence of green space can help reduce gun violence in a community, though its impact depends on where the space is located.

The study notes that physical surroundings influence everything from personal well‑being to neighborhood safety. It finds that while green space can aid in preventing gun violence, its effectiveness varies with its location.
summary: A new study from The Ohio State University found that green space can help prevent gun violence in a community. The study found that the effect depends on the location of the green space.
author: Phys.org

title: Early Height Differences in First-Year Beech Trees Predict Survival in Forest Competition
content:
Early growth differences help explain which beech trees survive forest competition. In forest ecosystems, light, water, and nutrients are limited, especially during “mast years” when trees and shrubs produce unusually large crops of fruits, nuts, or seeds.  

During these periods, the race for growth intensifies. Researchers are investigating whether small height differences—just one or two centimeters (0.4 or 0.8 inches)—between beech trees in their first year of life can influence their long‑term survival.
summary: In forest competition, light, water, and nutrients are limited, especially during mast years when trees and shrubs produce unusually large crops of fruits, nuts, or seeds. Scientists are examining whether height differences of one or two centimeters (0.4 or 0.8 inches) in the first year influence future survival.
author: Phys.org

title: Multiple Dating Apps May Reduce Anxiety for Gay Men
content:
Looking for relief from dating app anxiety? Try a variety of platforms

A recent observation suggests that gay men who use multiple dating apps experience lower levels of anxiety. The approach involves using more than one type of app, combining mainstream services such as Tinder or Hinge with gay‑specific platforms like Grindr.

By diversifying the platforms they engage with, users may find a more balanced and less stressful dating experience. This strategy could help reduce the anxiety often associated with mobile dating for gay men.
summary: Using more than one type of app could lead to lower levels of anxiety among gay men who use mobile dating platforms. This includes using both mainstream apps such as Tinder or Hinge and gay apps like Grindr.
author: Phys.org

title: UQ study maps pathway to develop heat‑adapted chickpeas using omic data
content:
A University of Queensland study has outlined a practical pathway for accelerating the development of heat‑adapted chickpeas using data from new “omic” technologies.  

The research team highlighted how these advanced tools can help scientists better understand the complex trait of heat tolerance in the crop.  

Ph. D. Candidate Callum Jamie said the suite of technologies offered tremendous opportunities to understand how a complex trait like heat tolerance works.
summary: A University of Queensland study outlined a practical pathway to accelerate development of heat‑adapted chickpeas using data from new omic technologies. Ph. D. Candidate Callum Jamie said the suite of technologies offers tremendous opportunities to understand how heat tolerance works.
author: Phys.org

title: New study disputes claim GST disproportionately burdens low‑income households
content:
New research challenges the notion that a goods and services tax (GST) always impacts lower‑income households the most.  

GST is incorporated into a wide range of everyday purchases, including groceries, clothing, restaurant meals and household bills. Because the tax is embedded in these items, any adjustment to GST rates can influence the amount of money households have available for other spending.
summary: New research challenges the idea that the goods and services tax always hits lower‑income households hardest. The GST is included in many everyday purchases such as groceries, clothing, restaurant meals and household bills, so changes to the tax can affect how much households have left to spend.
author: Phys.org

title: Climate Scientists Introduce Five Shared Socioeconomic Pathway Scenarios
content:
A decade ago, climate scientists introduced the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs), a set of five scenarios designed to explore future socioeconomic development. The SSPs were created to help model how societies might evolve under varying conditions of climate adaptation and mitigation.

Each scenario outlines a distinct pathway for socioeconomic progress, taking into account different levels of challenge to climate adaptation and mitigation efforts. The framework allows researchers to assess how these divergent paths could influence climate outcomes and public health impacts.
summary: About a decade ago, a group of climate scientists described five scenarios for the future. These scenarios, called the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs), suggest how socioeconomic development could evolve in worlds with differing challenges to climate adaptation and mitigation.
author: Phys.org

title: Physicists explain direction-dependent dielectric response in confined water
content:
Mehdi Neek-Amal and Francois Peeters at the University of Antwerp have identified the origins of a direction-dependent effect in water confined to a narrow gap between two plates. The physicists used an advanced mathematical model to analyze how this confined water responds to electric fields.

Their research, published in Physical Review Letters, demonstrates that two drastically different dielectric responses emerge from the natural bonding behavior of water molecules.
summary: Researchers at the University of Antwerp used a new mathematical model to reveal the origins of an unusual direction-dependent effect in water confined between two plates. Their study in Physical Review Letters showed that two different dielectric responses arise from the natural bonding behavior of water molecules.
author: Phys.org

title: AI surveillance at work provides minute‑by‑minute activity and productivity reports
content:
Artificial intelligence is transforming workplace surveillance by processing vast amounts of data to generate minute-by-minute accounts of employee activity and productivity. This evolution builds on historical monitoring methods, which have progressed from simple output targets to computer software commonly referred to as “bossware.”

UK technology editor Robert Booth discusses the current landscape of AI surveillance in an interview with Ian Sample. Booth details which sectors are adopting these advanced monitoring systems and the reasons behind their implementation. He also addresses the potential for these technologies to be counterproductive for employers.
summary: Workers have always been monitored by bosses through output targets and software called bossware, but AI now processes huge volumes of data to give minute‑by‑minute accounts of activity and productivity. UK technology editor Robert Booth explains which sectors are adopting this approach, why they are doing it, and how it could be counterproductive.
author: Guardian Science

title: Ito: A New Lua Library for Building Terminal User Interfaces
content:
Two developers have released Ito, a terminal user interface (TUI) library written in Lua, alongside a companion harness named Uji. The creators, who describe themselves as "Neovim nerds," chose Lua over JavaScript to allow for a minimal core design where every built-in abstraction and provider definition can be handled in Lua. The project is also capable of being based in Rust to improve performance.

To demonstrate the library's capabilities, one of the developers created a custom canvas implementation of Ito, which was exported as WebAssembly to power an interactive website for experimenting with Lua-based UIs. The team also included an "llms.txt" file to support AI-assisted coding. The Ito library is available at github.com/uji-labs/ito, and the Uji harness is hosted at github.com/uji-labs/uji.
summary: Developers have released Ito, a library that allows users to build terminal user interfaces entirely in Lua. The project includes a custom canvas implementation that runs in the browser via WebAssembly for interactive experimentation.
author: Hacker News

title: Aidlc: Adaptive workflow steering rules for AI coding agents
content:
AWS Labs has released "aidlc-workflows," a project designed to provide adaptive workflow steering rules for AI coding agents. The initiative is hosted on GitHub and has generated discussion on the Hacker News platform.

The project has garnered 15 points and 14 comments from the Hacker News community, reflecting early interest in its approach to managing AI-driven coding workflows.
summary: Aidlc introduces adaptive workflow steering rules for AI coding agents. The project is available on GitHub and has been discussed on Hacker News with 15 points and 14 comments.

content:
Show HN: Unfenced – Land for sale that borders public land

title: Pig kidneys rewarmed from -150°C freeze, work again for first time
content:
Scientists have successfully rewarmed pig kidneys that were cooled to -150 °C and stored in a freezer for months, demonstrating that the organs can function again. This achievement marks the first time such a process has been successfully completed, with the kidneys maintained in a glass-like state during storage.

The researchers hope to apply these findings to human organs in the future. The pig kidneys used in the study are similar in size to human kidneys.
summary: Scientists rewarmed pig kidneys that had been cooled to -150 °C and stored for months, and the organs worked again for the first time. The kidneys, similar in size to human ones, were left in a glass‑like state, and the researchers hope to replicate the findings with human organs.

title: Six wild ideas for perpetuating your mind
content: The human sense of self-awareness is deeply connected to the brain, a three-pound organ containing billions of neurons and trillions of delicate connections. While science confirms the brain's role in defining individual identity, experts note that it remains difficult to fully explain the mechanisms behind self-awareness or pinpoint its exact location within the organ.
summary: The article discusses the role of the brain in identity and self‑awareness. It notes that while science links identity to the brain's structure, explaining self‑awareness remains challenging.

title: How much more can nuclear power plants give?
content:
Constellation, the largest nuclear operator in the United States, has announced plans to increase power output from its facilities. This move comes amid rising electricity demand, which has prompted efforts to maximize the capacity of existing power plants.

The announcement is part of a broader trend over the past few weeks, with nuclear power plants seeking to generate additional electricity to meet current market needs.
summary: In this age of rising electricity demand, people are trying to squeeze every last bit of power out of every power plant possible. Over the past few weeks, there’s been big news about nuclear power plants trying to do just that.

content:

title: Zero-Click Spyware Infects Phones via Targeted Ads, Citizen Lab Releases Evidence
content:
‘Nightmare Scenario’: Zero‑Click Spyware Is Infecting Phones via Targeted Ads

Researchers at The Citizen Lab have for the first time released technical evidence that sophisticated mercenary spyware is being distributed through online advertising. The evidence shows the spyware can infect mobile phones without requiring any user interaction, using targeted ads as the delivery mechanism.
summary: Researchers at The Citizen Lab released technical evidence that sophisticated mercenary spyware is being distributed via online advertising. The spyware, described as zero-click, infects phones via targeted ads.

content: Democrats are preparing to investigate the Trump administration, but officials warn the effort may prove difficult. A recent government report on DOGE indicates that even obtaining basic information from the former administration will put a new Congress to the test.

title: Big Walk skips Xbox release to support BDS boycott of Microsoft
content:
Big Walk, a co‑op multiplayer walking adventure that launched in August, has become popular among players but has excluded Xbox users. The game's creators have now explained the reason for the exclusion.

Developer House House announced in a blog post that it chose not to release Big Walk on Xbox consoles to align with the Palestinian‑led BDS (Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions) movement. The BDS movement calls for a boycott of Microsoft, including products under its gaming division.

Microsoft was named a priority BDS target in June last year because of contracts it has with the Israeli military and government, with the boycott specifically calling out Xbox consoles.
summary: Developer House House has decided not to release Big Walk on Xbox consoles. The decision follows the Palestinian‑led BDS movement's call to boycott Microsoft, which includes Xbox products.
author: The Verge

title: Eiliko robot pet stores user data on Chinese servers, raising hack risk
content:
A new digital pet, a marshmallow‑shaped robot named Eiliko, has been sold on Amazon and marketed as a mood‑matching companion. According to a Verge article, the toy can change its cartoon expressions to reflect a user’s emotions and is designed for use over Wi‑Fi.

However, the Verge report warns that when the device is connected to the internet, it “phones home to China.” The AI companion can store everything a user says on Chinese servers, where the Verge notes that hackers could potentially gain access or hijack the device’s personality. The company that produces Eiliko, Energize Lab, is described in the article as appearing unconcerned about these security risks.

The author of the Verge piece purchased an Eiliko on August 29 and engaged in a 10‑minute conversation the following day. During that dialogue, the user asked the robot, “Do you ever tell anybody else what I’m saying?” and the toy replied, “Your secrets are safe with me.” The article concludes with a link to read the full story on The Verge.
summary: The Eiliko digital pet, made by Energize Lab, records conversations and saves them on servers in China. The Verge reports the data could be accessed or hijacked by hackers, and the company shows little concern.
author: The Verge

title: Amazon launches updated Bee Frontier and new Bee Eclipse wearable
content:
Amazon has expanded its Bee line of always‑listening AI wearables. The company acquired the startup last year and is now launching two new devices along with a subscription service.

The first product, the Bee Frontier, is priced at $74.99 and is an updated version of the original $50 Bee wearable. The second, the Bee Eclipse, will retail for $99.99 and is a credit‑card‑shaped gadget that snaps magnetically onto the back of a smartphone.

Both devices are marketed as tools to help users stay present. They record daily conversations and then generate summaries, transcripts, insights, and to‑do lists based on what they hear. Amazon is pairing the devices with a new subscription offering.
summary: Amazon announced two new Bee devices, the $74.99 Bee Frontier and the $99.99 Bee Eclipse. Both devices record conversations and provide summaries, transcripts, insights, and to‑dos.
author: The Verge

title: Ledger Launches Android-Based Atom Hardware Wallet Amid Southeast Asia Sales Halt
content:
Ledger has unveiled its newest crypto‑centric hardware effort, the Android‑based Atom. The device looks like a regular smartphone but is intended to be used alongside a phone rather than replace it.

The launch comes amid a challenging period for Ledger, which has had to stop selling some of its hardware in southeast Asia after a supply‑chain tampering incident that reportedly resulted in more than $86 million worth of cryptocurrency being stolen from users' accounts. Unlike Ledger’s earlier compact wallets that run custom software and often feature E Ink displays, the Atom is the spitting image of a standard Android smartphone.
summary: Ledger has announced its latest crypto‑centric hardware effort, the Android-based Atom, a device that resembles a phone but is instead designed to be used alongside one. It arrives at a tricky time for Ledger, which has been forced to cease sales of some of its hardware across southeast Asia following hardware tampering in its supply chain, which has reportedly seen over $86 million worth of crypto stolen from across some users' accounts.
author: The Verge

title: Amazon-owned Bee launches two new personal AI devices starting at $74.99
content:
Amazon‑owned Bee has introduced its first new AI devices since being acquired, launching an updated wearable and a credit‑card‑sized recorder that attaches to smartphones.  

The devices can summarize conversations, create to‑do lists, and integrate with Alexa and Amazon shopping. Prices for the new products start at $74.99.
summary: Amazon-owned Bee has released its first new AI devices since its acquisition, including an updated wearable and a credit-card-sized recorder that attaches to smartphones. The devices can summarize conversations, create to-do lists, and integrate with Alexa and Amazon shopping, with prices starting at $74.99.

content:

The tech market sell‑off deepens amid fears over rising inflation and potential interest rate hikes. Chip makers and tech investors such as Samsung and SoftBank plunged as the prospect of higher rates spooked markets.

An accelerating sell‑off of AI‑linked shares has hit global markets, with traders wary of the heavily indebted sector. summary: Chip makers and tech investors including Samsung and SoftBank fell sharply as worries over potential interest rate hikes spooked markets. South Korea’s Kospi 200 index dropped over 8% to a six‑month low, triggering circuit breakers and halting trading at times.

title: OpenAI sues former employee for leaking unreleased Apple product files
content:
OpenAI has filed a new claim in a lawsuit against Apple, alleging that a former employee who moved from the ChatGPT maker to the tech giant leaked confidential plans for an unreleased device. The filing, submitted in U.S. federal court in San Jose, California, states that the employee sent more than 100 files about the product to a personal account and later delivered a presentation on the same unreleased device to senior Apple leadership.

According to the lawsuit, the presentation took place months before the current legal dispute and Apple is now developing its own AI products, citing the recent release of Apple’s HomeView product. The claim adds a new layer of tension to the ongoing court proceedings between the two companies.
summary: OpenAI filed a lawsuit in US federal court in San Jose claiming a former employee who moved to Apple transferred over 100 files about an unreleased product to a personal account. The filing says the employee later presented the unreleased product to senior Apple leadership and notes Apple’s recent HomeView release as evidence of its AI work.
author: Guardian Technology

title: AI surveillance at work expands, causing stress for teachers at Euan Blair firm
content:
A new podcast titled “Is your boss watching you? The rise of AI surveillance at work” examines how artificial‑intelligence tools are expanding workplace monitoring. Historically, workers have been overseen through output targets and software dubbed “bossware,” but AI now processes massive data streams to generate minute‑by‑minute accounts of employee activity and productivity.

In the episode, Guardian journalist Ian Sample speaks with UK technology editor Robert Booth, who outlines the sectors adopting AI‑driven surveillance, the motivations behind its use, and the risk that such monitoring could become counterproductive. Booth also highlights reports from teachers at Euan Blair’s firm, who say the AI system used to rate their work has caused “horrendous stress.”
summary: Workers have long been monitored, and AI is now enhancing “bossware” to generate minute‑by‑minute activity and productivity data. In the podcast, Ian Sample speaks with UK technology editor Robert Booth about sectors adopting the technology, its motivations and possible counterproductivity, noting teachers at Euan Blair’s firm report ‘horrendous stress’ after AI rated their work.

title: OpenAI London staff earned average £2.3m each in salary and shares last year
content:
OpenAI’s London operation paid its employees an average of £2,318,181 each in the most recent year, according to the company’s accounts. The Westminster‑based subsidiary, OpenAI UK Ltd, reported that 110 staff shared £87 million in salaries and £168 million in share awards.

The firm, which is behind the ChatGPT product, is establishing a new headquarters in London’s King’s Cross district while continuing to operate from its Westminster office. OpenAI UK Ltd is preparing for a potential stock‑market listing at a valuation of roughly $1 trillion.
summary: Accounts for OpenAI UK Ltd show that 110 employees shared £87 million in salaries and £168 million in shares last year. The average compensation per staff member was £2,318,181.

title: At least two dead as heavy rain and flooding shut down Istanbul
content:
At least two people were killed after heavy rain and widespread flooding forced a shutdown of Istanbul, officials said.  

The Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality reported that some parts of the city experienced the highest amount of rain since 1985.  

The severe weather prompted authorities to halt activities across the metropolis as emergency measures were implemented.
summary: At least two people were killed after heavy rain and widespread flooding shut down Istanbul. The Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality said some areas received the highest rainfall since 1985.

content: A midday news bulletin released on October 15, 2026 offered a roundup of the most important stories from Europe and beyond. The bulletin highlighted the latest and breaking news across a range of topics, including world affairs, business, entertainment, politics, culture and travel.

title: FSB arrests Swedish citizen in Pskov on terrorism charges amid talk of prisoner swaps
content:
Moscow’s Federal Security Service (FSB) detained a Swedish citizen in the Pskov region on terrorism charges, while Japanese journalist Yuki Imai was arrested on Sakhalin on espionage charges. The arrests come days after former president Dmitry Medvedev wrote that Russia may need to “fill up the exchange pool with European and American idiots” to secure the release of Russians held abroad.

The timing of the detentions suggests Moscow is positioning the two foreign nationals for potential future prisoner swaps, according to the context of Medvedev’s comments. No further details on the individuals’ identities or the specific allegations were provided.
summary: The FSB arrested a Swedish citizen in Russia's Pskov region on terrorism charges and journalist Yuki Imai on Sakhalin on espionage charges. The arrests came days after former president Medvedev wrote that Russia may need to “fill up the exchange pool with European and American idiots” to recover Russians abroad.

title: Israel and Iran hold rare confidence‑building summit in Baku, Azerbaijan says hub
content:
Israel and Iran met in Baku for a rare “confidence‑building measures” summit, an event described by Azerbaijan as a connecting hub in the Eurasian space.  

The summit brought together the two Middle‑East rivals in Azerbaijan’s capital, marking an uncommon diplomatic engagement between the in‑conflict parties. Azerbaijan highlighted the meeting as evidence of its role as a regional bridge.  

Azerbaijan’s officials said the gathering underscores Baku’s position as a hub linking Eurasian nations.
summary: Israel and Iran met in Baku for a rare “confidence‑building measures” summit. Azerbaijan said the meeting shows the city is a connecting hub in the Eurasian space.

title: Oxfam France launches legal challenge alleging tax reforms favor wealthy
content:
Paris – French poverty has reached its highest level in decades and hunger is on the rise, according to a headline highlighting the impact of President Emmanuel Macron’s economic policies.  

Oxfam France is contesting the state’s tax system on constitutional grounds, saying that recent fiscal reforms have mainly benefited the wealthiest and deepened economic inequality. Director of Advocacy Nicolas Vercken told a gathering hosted by Charles Pellegrin that the issue is “not so much about how much the percentage of tax and the burden of our tax system, it’s who you tax and for what.”  

The organization has launched a legal initiative to determine whether the French government has failed to meet its constitutional obligations, a move that could place fiscal inequality under judicial review for years.
summary: Nicolas Vercken, Director of Advocacy for Oxfam France, said the organization is challenging the French state's constitutional obligations over tax inequality, arguing that successive fiscal reforms have disproportionately benefited the wealthiest. The legal initiative seeks to place fiscal inequality under judicial scrutiny for years to come.
author: France 24

title: Companies rent sensor‑equipped spy planes worldwide for political missions
content:
Companies around the world are leasing aircraft equipped with advanced sensors to military and intelligence customers for political missions, according to a recent analysis of the global spy‑plane market. The rentals span locations from the Mexican border to Syria and the Sahel region.

The market operates with a low public profile, yet its activities are observable across these diverse theatres. The demand for sensor‑laden planes underscores the role of private providers in supporting armed forces and intelligence services worldwide.
summary: Companies are renting out planes equipped with powerful sensors to armies and intelligence services from the Mexican border to Syria and the Sahel. The spy plane market is discreet but not invisible.

title: China and North Korea open Yalu River Bridge linking Dandong and Sinuiju
content:
China and North Korea formally opened the Yalu River Bridge on Thursday, linking the Chinese city of Dandong with the North Korean city of Sinuiju.  

Beijing said the new crossing is intended to promote economic and trade cooperation between the two nations.  

The bridge now provides a direct connection across the Yalu River between Dandong and Sinuiju.
summary: China and North Korea formally opened the Yalu River Bridge on Thursday, connecting Dandong in China with Sinuiju in North Korea. Beijing says the bridge will promote economic and trade cooperation.

title: US Defense Secretary announces plan to livestream firing‑squad execution of Fort Hood shooter
content:
U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced last week that the government intends to livestream the firing‑squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan. The proposal has sparked a backlash from Republicans in Congress, religious leaders and international observers.

Death‑penalty experts note that a government execution has never been broadcast or livestreamed, and the U.S. military has not carried out a firing‑squad execution since 1945, making the plan an unprecedented move. France 24’s International Affairs commentator Douglas Herbert reported on the reaction.
summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced plans to livestream the firing‑squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan. The proposal has drawn backlash from Republicans in Congress, religious leaders and international observers, and experts note no U.S. execution has ever been broadcast and the military has not used a firing squad since 1945.
author: France 24

title: Zelensky says Ukraine will ignore Trump's ban on Russian refinery strikes
content:
Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Kyiv will no longer follow U.S. President Donald Trump’s request to refrain from striking Russian oil refineries. The statement, published on Thursday, comes as tensions rise between the two leaders over a U.S.–Russia diesel agreement.

Relations between Kyiv and Washington have deteriorated since last week, when Trump eased sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large quantities of diesel onto global markets. FRANCE 24 International Affairs Editor Angela Diffley reported on the growing dispute.
summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine will no longer abide by US President Donald Trump's demand not to strike Russian oil refineries. He made the remarks amid deepening tensions after Trump eased sanctions on Russia in a diesel agreement that released large amounts of diesel onto global markets.
author: France 24

title: Chad plans to withdraw from ICC, sparking worries about Sudan war crimes probes
content:
Chad announced in July that it intends to withdraw from the International Criminal Court, saying the court is inefficient and disproportionately targets African nations.  

The planned exit could hinder future ICC investigations into alleged war crimes linked to the conflict in neighbouring Sudan, as investigators are currently working with Sudanese refugees sheltering in eastern Chad.  

Humanitarian organisations continue to operate in the area, providing assistance to those displaced by the crisis, according to FRANCE 24’s Harold Girard.
summary: In July, Chad announced plans to withdraw from the International Criminal Court, accusing the court of inefficiency and of disproportionately targeting African nations. The move could complicate ICC investigations of alleged war crimes in the neighbouring Sudan conflict, as investigators work with Sudanese refugees in eastern Chad.
author: France 24

title: Starlink disruption in Ukraine amid US pressure and Musk's closer ties to Trump
content:
SpaceX’s Starlink satellite internet service was recently disrupted in Ukraine, a development that coincides with increased pressure from Washington on Kyiv to cease its strikes against Russian oil refineries.  

Starlink is identified as a key component of Ukraine’s long‑range drone operations, and the interruption of the service has prompted questions about the potential impact on those capabilities.  

The situation also highlights growing attention to Elon Musk’s increasingly close ties with Donald Trump, as observers consider how the relationship might influence the disruption and its broader implications for Ukraine.
summary: SpaceX’s Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine was recently disrupted. The disruption occurs as Washington pressures Kyiv to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries and comes amid Elon Musk’s increasingly close ties with Donald Trump.

title: North Korea and China open New Yalu River Bridge after 12-year delay
content:

Officials described the opening as the latest indication of warming ties between the two neighboring nations.

content:
Romania: 2 ships on fire in Black Sea, 7 crew missing

Two chemical tankers have caught fire in Romanian territorial waters in the Black Sea. The blazes occurred after Russian drones were sighted in Romanian airspace, and seven crew members are missing.
summary: Two chemical tankers caught fire in Romanian territorial waters in the Black Sea. The blazes occurred after Russian drones were sighted in Romanian airspace.

title: WHO calls for faster action to curb lead exposure killing 3.5 million annually
content:
The World Health Organization (WHO) called on governments on Thursday to speed up measures that prevent lead exposure.  

WHO said lead exposure is estimated to cause more than 3.5 million deaths worldwide each year and to affect hundreds of millions of children.  

The agency urged countries to accelerate their efforts to end the health impacts of lead.
summary: The World Health Organization said on Thursday that countries must accelerate efforts to prevent lead exposure. WHO estimates lead exposure causes more than 3.5 million deaths globally each year and affects hundreds of millions of children.

title: Senegal detains over 320 LGBTQ+ individuals amid tightened anti-homosexuality law
content:
LGBTQ+ individuals in Senegal are increasingly going into hiding as a wave of arrests targets the community, according to a new Human Rights Watch (HRW) report.  

The report, citing the HIV Justice Network, says more than 320 people have been detained on accusations of “acts against nature” since February, following the recent tightening of Senegal’s law criminalising homosexuality. The crackdown includes mass arrests, forced HIV testing and obstacles to obtaining legal representation.  

Among those detained, at least 84 have been charged with “voluntary HIV transmission” on the sole basis of their HIV status. The HRW report documents these actions as part of an escalating campaign against LGBTQ+ people in the country.
summary: At least 320 people have been arrested in Senegal for alleged "acts against nature" since February, according to the Human Rights Watch report. The crackdown includes forced HIV testing and charges of voluntary HIV transmission, with 84 individuals charged solely because of their HIV status.
author: Guardian World

title: Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia may be delayed a year amid Houthi attacks
content:
The Asian Cup scheduled to take place in Saudi Arabia may be postponed by a year amid Houthi attacks, according to the AFC president.  

The tournament is set to begin on January 7, but the AFC president said it could be moved by a year if necessary.

title: FIFA to ban overturning of match suspensions after Balogun red‑card row

content:

content:
West Indies batsman Shai Hope said he was “worried about excess baggage” after receiving the latest Player of the Match award in the thrilling India‑West Indies series.

title: Obama says drift towards extremism not inevitable as 12,000 attend city venue
content:
Former US President Barack Obama said that a drift toward extremism “is not inevitable,” emphasizing his view that the world can avoid such a trajectory.  

More than 12,000 people filled a major venue in the city to hear Obama’s remarks on the challenges the world is facing.

title: Brazil Congress approves shorter working week, seen as win for Lula
content:
Brazil’s Congress approved a measure to shorten the working week, a development described as a win for President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.  

Supporters of Lula said the legislation could increase his popularity as the country heads toward a presidential run‑off scheduled in ten days.
summary: Brazil's Congress approved a shorter working week. Lula's supporters hope the measure will boost his popularity ahead of a presidential run‑off in 10 days.
author: BBC World

title: Russia accuses Ukraine of oil refinery attack as Zelensky says strikes will resume
content:
Russia has charged Ukraine with carrying out an attack on an oil refinery, a claim that follows Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky’s announcement that a pause on striking energy sites is ending.

Zelensky said the suspension of attacks on Russian energy infrastructure would be lifted after fresh Russian attacks, signaling a resumption of strikes against such targets.
summary: Russia alleges that Ukraine attacked an oil refinery. Ukraine's president Zelensky says the pause on striking energy sites is over after fresh Russian attacks.

title: SpaceX delivers over 6,000 pounds of cargo to ISS with CRS-35 Dragon
content:
SpaceX’s CRS‑35 cargo Dragon is scheduled to rendezvous with the International Space Station today, October 15, after a two‑day chase. The spacecraft will deliver more than 6,000 pounds of cargo to the orbiting laboratory.

The launch and docking will be available for live viewing.
summary: SpaceX's CRS-35 cargo Dragon will rendezvous with the International Space Station today (Oct. 15) after a two-day chase. The launch will be broadcast live for viewers to watch.

title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
content:
Lisandro Martínez has publicly criticized Manchester United’s ownership, arguing that the club’s problems stem from deeper issues than individual player mistakes. In a recent appearance on Amazon Prime, Martínez said the team’s “indifferent start to the season” is partly due to his own high‑profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham.

The defender’s remarks came after United’s 2‑0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night. Martínez appeared in a hot‑dog costume and mocked innocence while discussing the loss, suggesting that the club’s struggles go beyond on‑field performance.

Former United players reacted to Martínez’s comments. Wayne Rooney called him “disrespectful,” Ashley Young said he “doesn’t feel like he’s got the right,” and Rio Ferdinand noted on his podcast that “These things don’t end well, man.”
summary: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the clubHeartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season, given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it.

title: Papua New Guinea's Rugby League Brings Unity to 800-Language Nation Ahead of World Cup
content:
World Cup co‑hosts Papua New Guinea celebrate their love of rugby league through the national teams of the Kumuls and the Orchids. The sport’s popularity is evident in the pride and unity these teams inspire across the island.

The Kumuls and Orchids serve as badges of hope and unity for Papua New Guinea, a nation of 800 languages, during the upcoming World Cup.
summary: Papua New Guinea, a World Cup co-host, is known for its love of rugby league. The Kumuls and the Orchids national teams are badges of hope and unity for the island's 800 languages.

title: European figures urge Arsene Wenger to challenge Infantino for Fifa presidency
content:
Senior figures in European football have expressed a desire for former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger to enter the race for the Fifa presidency. According to BBC Sport, these influential individuals view Wenger as a potential surprise candidate who could challenge the current incumbent, Gianni Infantino.

The proposal suggests a significant shift in the leadership dynamics of world football, positioning Wenger as a direct contender against Infantino.
summary: Senior figures in European football have told BBC Sport that they want former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger to run as a surprise candidate. They specifically want him to run against Gianni Infantino for the Fifa presidency.

title: Cait Conley urges Rep. Mike Lawler not to mansplain domestic abuse
content: Democrat Cait Conley instructed Republican Rep. Mike Lawler not to “mansplain” to her about domestic abuse during a televised debate on Wednesday night. The exchange occurred as the candidates discussed an alleged gang rape that took place at a Cornell University fraternity in 2024. The debate was moderated by a representative from PIX11 News, an affiliate of Nexstar Media Group.
summary: Democrat Cait Conley told Rep. Mike Lawler (R-N. Y.) during a televised debate on Wednesday night not to mansplain her about domestic abuse. The debate covered an alleged gang rape at a Cornell University fraternity in 2024.
