title: James Talarico Holds CNN‑Jubilee Town Hall to Urge Ken Paxton Debate
content:
Texas Democrat James Talarico held a town hall on Wednesday, taking questions from voters in a session hosted by CNN and Jubilee. The event featured Talarico on stage alone as he urged his Republican rival, Gov. Ken Paxton, to join him in a debate amid the closely watched Senate race.

Talarico, a state lawmaker and Presbyterian seminarian, used the forum to emphasize unity, stating “we’re all on the same team.” He called for a direct debate with Paxton, arguing that such a discussion would benefit the electorate in the competitive Senate contest.
summary: Texas Democrat James Talarico, a state lawmaker and Presbyterian seminarian, took questions from voters during a town hall hosted by CNN and Jubilee on Wednesday. He urged rival Republican Ken Paxton to debate in their closely watched Senate race.
author: The Hill

title: Trump’s approval rating hits record low in Fox News poll
content: A new Fox News survey indicates that President Trump’s overall approval rating has reached a record low for either of his terms. The poll reflects growing voter dissatisfaction with his management of key issues, with 36 percent of respondents approving of his overall handling of the presidency. Conversely, 64 percent of respondents disapproved of his performance.
summary: A Fox News survey found President Trump’s overall approval rating at a record low, with 36% approval and 64% disapproval. The decline reflects growing voter dissatisfaction with his handling of key issues.
author: The Hill

title: Trump questions US negotiators' identity in Iran talks at Montana rally
content:
President Trump expressed uncertainty at a rally in Montana on Wednesday night about who U.S. officials were negotiating with in efforts to end the Iran war. “I don’t know who the hell we’re negotiating with,” he said.

He added that the group in question “don’t have a navy. They don’t have an air force. Their army is decimated. Their leaders are gone,” referencing the state of the Iranian military and leadership.
summary: President Trump stated at a Montana rally that he was unsure who U.S. officials were negotiating with to end the Iran war. He claimed Iran's military forces are decimated and its leaders are gone.
author: The Hill

title: NHS Diagnosis Gap: Fewer Than 1 in 15 South London Teens with Mental Disorders
content:
A new study from the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience (IoPPN) at King's College London estimates that fewer than one in 15 young people in south London who have a mental health disorder may have received a diagnosis from NHS mental health services.

The research highlights a gap between the prevalence of mental health disorders among south London teens and the proportion that are formally diagnosed by NHS services.
summary: A new study by the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience at King's College London found that fewer than one in 15 young people in south London who have a mental health disorder may have received a diagnosis from NHS mental health services. The study highlights a significant gap in NHS diagnosis coverage for these teens.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Large MRI dataset reveals consistent adolescent brain wiring patterns
content:
Researchers have developed a large, openly available neuroimaging resource comprising more than 24,000 MRI scans from over 10,000 adolescents. This dataset offers insights into how the brain’s wiring develops during the adolescent years.

To compile the resource, the team utilized advanced, open-source image-processing methods. These techniques allowed them to identify highly consistent patterns of development across 21 distinct study sites, successfully accounting for variations in scanner technology and image quality.
summary: Researchers released an openly available neuroimaging resource that includes more than 24,000 MRI scans of over 10,000 adolescents, mapping brain wiring changes during adolescence. Advanced open-source image-processing methods revealed highly consistent developmental patterns across 21 study sites, despite variations in scanner technology and image quality.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Purdue scientist uses lasers and Doppler effect to personalize chemotherapy
content:
Purdue University scientist David Nolte is developing an imaging system that could tailor chemotherapy to individual tumors. The system uses laser light, the Doppler effect, and artificial intelligence to assess how a specific cancer responds to various drugs.

Nolte’s approach aims to provide early insight into tumor drug sensitivity, a step that could improve treatment outcomes as the number of available chemotherapy agents grows. By identifying the most effective drug for each patient’s unique cancer, the technology seeks to personalize therapy and reduce trial‑and‑error.

The project is still in development, but it represents a new direction in cancer treatment research that focuses on the individuality of each tumor.
summary: Purdue University scientist David Nolte is developing an imaging system that utilizes laser light, the Doppler effect, and AI. The technology aims to provide early insight into how individual tumors respond to specific chemotherapy drugs.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Parents of kids who need complex medical care at home tend to resolve frequent safety issues on their own, study finds
content:
A study published in the journal Pediatrics by researchers from Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago highlights the challenges faced by parents of medically complex children. Approximately one in 20 U.S. children under the age of 18 are considered medically complex, a classification that includes those with multiorgan system conditions such as cerebral palsy who rely on implanted tube-related medical technology.

These children receive the majority of their care at home, placing the responsibility on parents to manage complicated devices and intricate medication and nutrition regimens. The study found that while these parents frequently encounter safety challenges in this role, they typically develop creative solutions to address these issues without involving the child's care team.
summary: Approximately 1 in 20 U. S.
author: Medical Xpress

title: STING Pathway Identified as Potential Target to Treat Age-Related Bone Loss
content:
Researchers are exploring the STING signaling pathway as a possible target for treating bone loss that occurs with aging.  

Osteoporosis, the condition that makes bones weak and brittle, is driven by changes in the cells of the bone marrow microenvironment.  These changes include elevated fat and immune cells that promote inflammation.  

The STING pathway is known to drive inflammation, but its role in aging bones has until now been unclear.
summary: Osteoporosis, the age-related weakening of bones, is driven by changes in bone marrow cells, including increased fat and inflammation-promoting immune cells. The STING signaling pathway is a molecular driver of inflammation, but its role in aging bones has been unclear until recent research.
author: Medical Xpress

title: 143 of 154 Developing Countries Have National Adaptation Plans, Implementation Lagging
content:
Climate adaptation's delivery gap: Turning national plans into action

By 2025, 143 of 154 developing countries had established a National Adaptation Plan process. Despite this progress, implementation has not kept pace with the plans.

Many countries still lack the institutional capacity, project preparation, and finance needed to transform their priorities into actionable strategies, bankable projects, and tangible results on the ground.
summary: By 2025, 143 of 154 developing countries had a National Adaptation Plan process in place. However, many still lack the institutional capacity, project preparation, and finance needed to implement these plans into actionable projects and results.
author: Phys.org

title: Galapagos Marine Iguanas Face Survival Threat from Black‑Market Trafficking Amid Super El Niño
content:
Scientists warn that the Galapagos marine iguana, the only lizard capable of living and foraging at sea, may face a survival crisis.  

International researchers report that black‑market trafficking of these iguanas is peaking at the same time that a super El Niño event is decimating their natural food sources.
summary: International scientists warn that black‑market trafficking of Galapagos marine iguanas is peaking. The super El Niño is decimating their natural food source, threatening their survival.
author: Phys.org

title: CSIRO report finds growing options to cut on-farm emissions
content:
A new report by CSIRO, Australia’s national science agency, has identified investment priorities for low‑emissions agriculture.  

The report finds a growing suite of promising options already available to reduce on‑farm emissions.  

It also highlights further opportunities for practical solutions that Australian producers can adopt.
summary: CSIRO, Australia's national science agency, found a growing suite of promising options already available to reduce on-farm emissions. The report also identifies further opportunities for practical solutions for Australian producers.
author: Phys.org

title: EIT Food Observatory Report: Consumers Need Clear Answers on Precision Fermentation
content:
Consumers may not fully understand precision fermentation yet, but many are curious enough to taste the results, according to new qualitative research from the EIT Food Consumer Observatory. The study, published ahead of World Food Day on Oct. 16, indicates that this curiosity presents a significant opportunity for food innovation.

The research emphasizes that companies must answer consumers’ questions clearly and deliver a satisfying first bite to build trust. The findings highlight the importance of transparency and product quality in the growing precision fermentation market.
summary: Qualitative research from the EIT Food Consumer Observatory, published ahead of World Food Day on Oct. 16, shows consumers are curious about precision fermentation but lack clear understanding. The study suggests companies must answer questions clearly and deliver on the first bite to turn curiosity into an opportunity for food innovation.
author: Phys.org

title: Ascension Island's planting project creates lush cloud forest
content:
Ascension Island: How a planting project created a lush cloud forest

In the middle of nowhere, a small island emerges in the Atlantic Ocean. This unique territory completely changed in the 19th century thanks to the efforts of two British scientists: Charles Darwin and Joseph Dalton Hooker.  

Both researchers stopped at the British naval base and documented the island during their expeditions. Their observations marked a significant moment in the island’s history.
summary: A planting project on Ascension Island created a lush cloud forest. The island’s 19th‑century transformation was documented by British scientists Charles Darwin and Joseph Dalton Hooker during their visits to the British naval base.
author: Phys.org

title: Russia and China use AI to launch relentless cyberattacks on UK
content:
Russia and China are employing artificial intelligence to conduct relentless cyberattacks against the United Kingdom, according to recent reports.  

The use of AI is accelerating the speed of these attacks on UK infrastructure, making them more rapid and potentially more damaging.  

At the same time, AI technologies are also being deployed to help defend the United Kingdom’s critical systems against such threats.
summary: Russia and China are using artificial intelligence to stage relentless cyberattacks against the UK. AI is increasing the speed of attacks on UK infrastructure while also being used to help defend against them.
author: New Scientist

title: Whalefall Review: Gruesome Film About Diver Swallowed by Sperm Whale
content:
Whalefall review: Worth watching for the bits inside a sperm whale

The film Whalefall, adapted from Daniel Kraus’s novel, follows a diver who is swallowed by a sperm whale. Critics describe the movie as terrifically gruesome, with intense and graphic scenes that highlight the perilous nature of the story.

Bethan Ackerley, in her review, notes that while the film delivers on visceral horror, it also leans heavily into sentimentality, which she finds excessive. The review suggests that viewers seeking the raw, shocking moments of the whale’s interior may find the film worthwhile, though the emotional tone may not appeal to everyone.
summary: The film, based on Daniel Kraus’s novel, follows a diver swallowed by a sperm whale. Bethan Ackerley calls it terrifically gruesome but far too sentimental.
author: New Scientist

title: Professor Eric So Discusses AI's Impact on Thinking in New Book
content:
A new book by Professor Eric So examines how technology influences thinking skills, framing the discussion as a “collision” between artificial intelligence, the human brain, and society. The work is presented in a Q&A format that probes the ways AI interacts with cognition and social structures.

So’s analysis focuses on the impact of AI on mental processes, exploring how emerging tools reshape the way people think and learn. The book aims to illuminate the broader implications of this technological intersection for individuals and communities.
summary: Professor Eric So has published a new book that examines how AI technology affects thinking skills. The book explores the collision between AI, the brain, and society.
author: MIT News

title: Cancers Rising Faster in Younger English Adults, Scientists Seek New Causes
content:
A major study has identified that several cancers are increasing more rapidly among younger adults in England, even as traditional risk factors such as smoking, diet and other established contributors have generally improved.  

The analysis found that excess weight accounts for only a portion of the rise, prompting researchers to investigate additional explanations. Potential factors under consideration include alterations in the gut microbiome and exposures experienced early in life.  

Scientists acknowledge that the reasons for the accelerating cancer rates in younger populations remain incompletely understood.
summary: A major study found that several cancers are rising faster among younger adults in England, even as smoking, diet, and other established risk factors have generally improved. Excess weight explains only part of the increase, leaving scientists searching for other possible causes such as changes in the gut microbiome and early-life exposures.
author: Science Daily

title: 47-year study finds fitness and strength start declining around age 35
content:
A 47‑year longitudinal study has identified a key milestone in physical aging, finding that fitness and strength start to decline around age 35. The research shows that this downturn occurs even among individuals who maintain regular exercise routines.

The investigators observed that the rate of decline speeds up as people grow older, indicating an accelerating loss of physical capacity over time. Despite the early onset of this decline, the study notes that beginning an exercise regimen in adulthood can still enhance overall physical performance.

These findings suggest that while age‑related strength loss begins in the mid‑30s, targeted physical activity later in life remains beneficial for maintaining functional ability.
summary: A 47-year study found that fitness and strength begin declining around age 35, even among regular exercisers. Researchers said the decline accelerates as people get older, but starting to exercise in adulthood can still improve physical performance.
author: Science Daily

title: 120‑million‑year‑old fossil uncovers new European megaraptoran dinosaur
content:
A 120‑million‑year‑old fossil that had lain forgotten in a museum for nearly a century has been identified as a new, fearsome dinosaur.  

The tiger‑sized predator, noted for its giant claws, was described as potentially more dangerous to humans than a Tyrannosaurus rex. Its remains constitute the first evidence of megaraptorans in Europe, offering insight into how this group of mysterious dinosaurs later evolved into gigantic hunters.  

The find expands the known diversity of European dinosaurs from the mid‑Cretaceous period.
summary: A 120‑million‑year‑old fossil forgotten in a museum for nearly a century revealed a new dinosaur. The tiger‑sized predator provides the first evidence of megaraptorans in Europe and may have been more dangerous to humans than a T. Rex.
author: Science Daily

title: Ozempic and Wegovy linked to slight risk of sudden vision loss
content:
Popular diabetes and weight‑loss medications Ozempic and Wegovy have been linked to a slightly increased risk of a rare condition that can cause sudden, potentially permanent vision loss, according to recent research.

Rutgers researchers noted that while the risk remains very low, the findings merit attention because millions of people are using GLP‑1 medications such as these drugs.
summary: Rutgers researchers found that the diabetes and weight‑loss drugs Ozempic and Wegovy are linked to a slightly increased risk of a rare condition that can cause sudden, potentially permanent vision loss. The risk is described as very low, but the researchers say the finding merits attention as millions use GLP‑1 medications.
author: Science Daily

title: Tropical fires spread to central and eastern Amazon during El Niño
content:
Fires have reached the central and eastern Amazon rainforest as part of a broader tropical blaze linked to the El Niño weather pattern.  

The cascade of fires began in equatorial Asia and then spread across the tropics, continuing into the Amazon region. The ongoing blazes are occurring during the current El Niño episode.
summary: During El Niño, a cascade of fires across the tropics began in equatorial Asia. The fires then continued in the central and eastern Amazon.

content:

Flipflop aims to provide fast file transfers, incorporates the Slint framework, and is designed to maintain a persistent communication channel with trusted external users that can remain continuously active. The post on Hacker News has received 22 points and generated seven comments.

title: Poland aims for economic growth as wages rise and living costs climb
content:
Poland is being portrayed as a nation that has risen economically since the Soviet era, with wages soaring even as the cost of living climbs, according to the final installment of a series on the country. The piece also raises questions about whether increased military spending will support or impede Poland’s growth and notes the country’s push for European Union energy resilience in response to Russian aggression.

From an observation deck atop the Varso tower in Warsaw, the city’s skyline includes the Soviet‑era Palace of Culture and Science, a building that continues to split public opinion. Some view the structure as a relic of oppression that should be removed, while others regard it as an iconic landmark and a stark reminder of history.
summary: Poles say wages have surged while the cost of living has also increased. The article also raises questions about the impact of military spending on growth and notes Poland’s push for EU energy resilience amid Russian aggression, referencing the divided views on the Soviet‑era Palace of Culture and Science.

title: Four-lane bridge linking China and North Korea opens after ten-year delay
content:
A new four‑lane bridge linking China and North Korea has opened, ending a project that was delayed for ten years.  

The opening occurs roughly one month after North Korea and Russia inaugurated a road bridge intended to strengthen their bilateral ties.
summary: A new four-lane bridge connecting China and North Korea has opened after a decade of delay. Its opening follows the opening of a road bridge between North Korea and Russia about a month earlier.

content:
Kaja Kallas, identified in the report as the EU’s top diplomat, spoke exclusively to Euronews presenter Maria Tadeo as EU leaders gathered in Brussels for the opening of a crucial summit.

title: Hundreds protest in Bangkok against IMF and World Bank meetings
content:
Hundreds of protesters marched through Bangkok on Thursday, 15 October, to voice opposition to the International Monetary Fund and World Bank’s annual meetings being held in the Thai capital.  

The demonstrators decried the two institutions and warned that their policies promote “destructive capitalism.”  

The rally coincided with the scheduled IMF and World Bank gatherings in Bangkok.

title: Thousands protest across Colombia against President Abelardo de la Espriella's policies
content:
Thousands of Colombians marched peacefully across the country on Wednesday, protesting against the policies of right‑wing President Abelardo de la Espriella. The demonstrations marked the opposition’s first major show of force since he took office in August.

In Bogotá, former leftist president Gustavo Petro led a rally that drew trade unionists, Indigenous groups, students, and feminist activists. The protestors gathered to voice their concerns about the new administration’s direction.
summary: Thousands of Colombians protested peacefully across the country on Wednesday against right‑wing President Abelardo de la Espriella, marking the opposition’s first major demonstrations since he took office in August. Former leftist president Gustavo Petro led a rally in Bogota that was joined by trade unionists, Indigenous groups, students and feminist activists.

title: EU leaders convene Thursday summit to seal €2 trillion 2028‑2034 budget by Christmas
content:
EU leaders are convening at a summit on Thursday to negotiate a deal on the European Union’s budget for 2028‑2034, which totals nearly €2 trillion. The negotiations aim to reach an agreement by Christmas.

The talks come amid deep divisions among member states over spending priorities and growing concerns that upcoming elections, especially in France, could bolster eurosceptic forces.
summary: EU leaders are heading to a Thursday summit to reach a deal on the European Union’s nearly €2 trillion budget for 2028‑2034. title: Russia strikes Izmail port and two cargo ships en route to Odesa
content:
Russia struck Ukraine’s Izmail port and hit two cargo ships traveling to Odesa, the Russian Defence Ministry said Thursday.  

A day earlier, Moscow launched additional missiles and drones at Ukrainian cities, reportedly knocking out power to hundreds of thousands of residents.  

The Defence Ministry’s statement was part of a live update on the ongoing conflict.
summary: Russia struck Ukraine's Izmail port and two cargo ships heading to Odesa, according to the Russian Defence Ministry. Earlier, Moscow launched missiles and drones that knocked out power to hundreds of thousands of Ukrainian residents.

title: PSG beat Manchester City 4-2 on Champions League Matchday 2
content:
Paris Saint‑Germain secured a 4‑2 win over Manchester City in a Champions League matchday 2 thriller, keeping them at the top of the group table.  

The French side dominated the first half, taking a 3‑0 advantage before the second half. Manchester City fought back, with Erling Haaland scoring twice to bring the score to 3‑2, but could not complete the comeback.  

PSG remain ahead of Barcelona in the league‑phase standings and will face the Spanish club next Tuesday.
summary: PSG defeated Manchester City 4-2 in the Champions League after leading 3-0 at halftime. The victory left PSG atop the league-phase table, ahead of Barcelona, whom they will face next Tuesday.

title: EU summit in Brussels to discuss China trade deficit, Ukraine and next budget
content:
EU leaders gathered in Brussels for a summit that will centre on relations with China, the situation in Ukraine and the European Union’s budget.  

The agenda includes examining measures to curb the bloc’s large trade deficit with China and seeking further agreement on the next EU budget ahead of major elections scheduled for next year.

title: Brazil Congress approves amendment limiting work week to 40 hours
content:
Brazil’s Congress has approved a constitutional amendment that bans six‑day workweeks, limiting the legal maximum to 40 hours per week. The change could affect up to 30 million workers and would give many employees an extra day off each week.

The amendment is seen as a political win for President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who has championed the measure in an effort to counter the first‑round lead of far‑right senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The vote comes just weeks before the presidential runoff.
summary: Brazil's Congress approved a constitutional amendment limiting the work week to a maximum of 40 hours, potentially affecting 30 million workers and providing a political win for President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva before the runoff. Lula has strongly championed the amendment, which would give some workers an extra day off each week.

title: Argentina's Milei backs Trump, says US midterm vote crucial for West
content:
Argentina’s President Javier Milei publicly endorsed former U.S. President Donald Trump for the upcoming U.S. midterm elections, describing the vote as “crucial for the West.” While accepting an award in Washington, Milei warned that conservatives “cannot give an inch” in Latin America.

Milei’s comments linked the U.S. election to broader regional strategy, emphasizing a hard‑line stance toward left‑leaning governments in the hemisphere. The remarks were made during the award ceremony, underscoring his alignment with the U.S. president’s agenda.
summary: Milei backed Donald Trump for the U.S. midterm elections and said the vote is crucial for the West. While accepting an award in Washington, he said conservatives cannot give an inch in Latin America.
author: Al Jazeera

title: X suspends 13,000 accounts, citing foreign influence before US midterms
content: X has suspended 13,000 accounts, saying the actions were taken because of alleged foreign influence ahead of the United States midterm elections. The social platform explained that networks had targeted political debate across the spectrum in the run‑up to the vote.
summary: X announced it has suspended 13,000 accounts, alleging foreign influence ahead of the US midterm elections. The platform said the networks targeted US political debate across the spectrum.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Heavy rain causes mass pileup in Sao Paulo's Anhangabau tunnel
content:
Heavy rain triggered a mass pileup in Brazil’s Anhangabau tunnel, according to reports. Flooding in the area caused vehicles to become stacked inside the tunnel, leaving drivers and passengers stranded.

The incident occurred in Sao Paulo’s Anhangabau tunnel, where the floodwaters forced cars to pile up and left people trapped within the tunnel. No further details on casualties or rescue efforts were provided.
summary: Heavy rain caused flooding in Sao Paulo’s Anhangabau tunnel. The flooding left vehicles piled up and people stranded inside the tunnel.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Governments urged to boost energy, food, finance tipping points at COP17 and COP31
content:
Governments attending COP17 and COP31 are being urged to accelerate positive tipping points in the sectors of energy, food and finance, according to the theme “Restoring nature is key to a more resilient future.”  

The call emphasizes that advancing these tipping points is essential for building resilience, with nature restoration highlighted as a central component of the strategy.
summary: At COP17 and COP31, governments must accelerate positive tipping points in energy, food and finance. Restoring nature is presented as key to a more resilient future.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Lamine Yamal's 17 goal contributions in 10 games surpass Messi's teenage record
content:
Lamine Yamal has recorded 17 goal contributions for Barcelona after just 10 games, a tally that exceeds the total Lionel Messi achieved during his Ballon d’Or‑winning season as a teenager.  

The comparison highlights Yamal’s early impact at the club, surpassing the teenage output of Messi in that award‑winning campaign.
summary: Lamine Yamal has recorded 17 goal contributions in his first 10 games for Barcelona. That total exceeds the number Messi achieved as a teenager during his Ballon d'Or‑winning season.
author: Al Jazeera

title: G20 finance ministers and central bankers meet in Thailand amid Iran war fallout
content: G20 finance ministers and central bankers assembled in Thailand as the fallout from the Iran war intensified. The officials met while the conflict has driven energy prices higher and heightened uncertainty across the global economy. The gathering reflects concerns about the war’s economic repercussions.
summary: G20 finance ministers and central bankers are meeting in Thailand as the fallout from the Iran war continues. The conflict is pushing energy prices higher and creating uncertainty for the global economy.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israel election on Oct. 27 watched across Africa for impact on ties
content:
Israel’s upcoming election on October 27 is being closely monitored across the continent, from Morocco to South Africa.  

Analysts say the vote could serve as a test of whether Israel’s diplomatic and economic relationships with African nations can endure the repercussions of the war on Gaza.  

The election’s outcome may therefore influence the stability of Israel’s ties throughout Africa.
summary: The Israeli election scheduled for October 27 is being closely observed from Morocco to South Africa. The vote could test whether Israel's ties with African countries withstand the fallout from the Gaza war.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Brooklyn novelty shop Art of Play says staff threatened after Kelly Clarkson complaint
content:
Brooklyn novelty shop Art of Play has become the focus of a dispute with singer Kelly Clarkson after the artist complained online about her treatment at the store over a mechanical bird.  

The shop says its employees have received threats following Clarkson’s public criticism.  

Art of Play confirmed the threats and noted the incident has placed the store at the centre of a “surreal” row with the singer.
summary: Art of Play, a Brooklyn novelty shop, is involved in a dispute with singer Kelly Clarkson over a mechanical bird. The shop says its staff have been threatened after Clarkson complained online about how she was treated.
author: BBC World

title: Orange haze blankets Palangka Raya as nearby wildfires rage
content:
Thick orange smog enveloped the Indonesian city of Palangka Raya, prompting residents to share footage of the haze blanketing the town, according to reports. The dense orange haze descended as nearby wildfires continued to rage.

The visual documentation highlights the extent of the air pollution affecting Palangka Raya while the surrounding fires remain active.
summary: Thick orange smog covered Palangka Raya, prompting Indonesians to share footage of the haze. The smog is linked to wildfires that continue raging nearby.
author: BBC World

title: White House defends new press secretary despite questions about bar registration
content:
The White House has defended its newly appointed press secretary after media reports raised questions about her legal credentials.  

Katie Zacharia, the new press secretary, does not appear to be registered to the legal bar in any state where she has lived.  

White House officials said the appointment remains appropriate despite the lack of bar registration.
summary: White House officials defended the appointment of new press secretary Katie Zacharia amid questions about her legal credentials. Zacharia does not appear to be registered to the legal bar in any state where she has lived.
author: BBC World

title: Retired US generals urge Pentagon to stop livestream of Nidal Hasan execution
content:
Seventy‑two retired U.S. generals have urged the Pentagon to cancel a planned livestream of the execution of Nidal Hasan, describing the broadcast as “barbaric.”  

In a letter, the former officers warned that livestreaming the execution “will taint the honor of the military that employs it, and a nation that allows it.”
summary: Seventy‑two former U.S. officers wrote a letter urging the Pentagon to cancel the planned livestream of Nidal Hasan’s execution. They said livestreaming the execution will “taint the honor of the military that employs it, and a nation that allows it.”
author: BBC World

title: West Ham defeat nine-man Lincoln 6-0 as Soucek scores twice
content:
West Ham United secured a 6-0 victory over Lincoln City at the ProAmpac Stadium, returning to winning ways in the Championship. The match was defined by early disciplinary issues for the hosts, as Tom Hamer was sent off after just three minutes and Conor McGrandles followed him off the pitch 20 minutes later, leaving Lincoln with nine men.

Konstantinos Mavropanos headed West Ham into the lead on the stroke of half-time. Tomas Soucek completed the scoring for the visitors, doubling his tally to finish the big win. Other Championship action included Portsmouth, who struck late to defeat a 10-man Sheffield United side.
summary: West Ham secured a 6-0 Championship victory against Lincoln, who were reduced to nine men after two red cards. Tomas Soucek scored twice to complete the win for the hosts.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Manchester City staff join government trade delegation to India
content:
A representative from Manchester City joined a government-backed trade delegation to India this week, despite the club’s recent conviction for 114 breaches of Premier League rules. The trip was organized by business secretary Jonathan Reynolds and included visits to Delhi and Mumbai.

Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig, who is the successor to Andy Burnham, led the delegation alongside other northern mayors. The group focused on promoting British trade and tourism during their stay in India.
summary: A Manchester City representative was invited on a government trade trip to India despite the club being found guilty of 114 Premier League rule breaches. Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig took the representative to Delhi and Mumbai on a delegation organized by business secretary Jonathan Reynolds.
author: Guardian Sport

title: CREW sues to bar Kushner from government role under Appointments Clause
content:
Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW) filed a lawsuit on Wednesday challenging the legality of Jared Kushner’s position within the Trump administration. The watchdog group’s legal action specifically targets Kushner’s role in his father-in-law’s government.

The lawsuit argues that Kushner is occupying a government position and exercising government authority in violation of the Appointments Clause. CREW stated that the primary objective of the suit is to bar Kushner from holding this office.
summary: Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington filed a lawsuit on Wednesday challenging the legality of Jared Kushner's role in the Trump administration. The suit seeks to bar Kushner from occupying his government position and exercising authority in violation of the Appointments Clause.
author: The Hill

title: Poll: 71% of Americans oppose live broadcast executions
content:
A new YouGov survey indicates that the majority of Americans oppose the public broadcasting of executions, a finding that emerges ahead of the Pentagon’s planned livestreamed execution of Nidal Hasan, the convicted Fort Hood shooter. The poll revealed that 71 percent of respondents opposed having executions broadcast live to the public.

In contrast, 18 percent of participants supported the practice, while 13 percent indicated they were unsure. The survey also noted differences in opinion along partisan lines.
summary: A YouGov poll found that 71 percent of Americans oppose having executions broadcast live to the public. This opposition exists ahead of the Pentagon’s planned livestreamed execution of convicted Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan.
author: The Hill

title: Vienna team finds Gas5 RNA regulates NUP98::KDM5A condensates in aggressive AML
content:
Researchers at the University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna, working with the CeMM Research Center for Molecular Medicine and St. Anna Children’s Cancer Research, have created a new analytical method that identifies RNA molecules involved in cancer‑promoting cellular structures.  

Using this method, the Vienna‑based team discovered that the RNA molecule Gas5 regulates NUP98::KDM5A oncogenic condensates, which control gene activity in aggressive forms of acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The findings offer a new starting point for cancer research and potential improvements in patient treatment.  

The study was published in the journal The EMBO Journal.
summary: Researchers at the University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna, together with the CeMM Research Center for Molecular Medicine and St. Anna Children's Cancer Research, developed a new analytical method to identify RNA molecules involved in cancer-promoting cellular structures. Using the method they identified the RNA molecule Gas5 as an important regulator of NUP98::KDM5A oncogenic condensates that control gene activity in aggressive forms of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and the study was published in The EMBO Journal.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Experts say 4,000 to 10,000 daily steps offer health benefits for weight loss
content:
Experts state that there is no single answer to how many steps are required daily for weight loss, despite the frequent repetition of the 10,000-step benchmark. While fitness trackers and smartwatches have become popular tools for monitoring activity to support health goals, specific step counts vary for individual results.

Research indicates that taking between 4,000 and 10,000 steps per day can provide health benefits, suggesting that lower activity levels may still contribute to positive outcomes.
summary: Experts state there is no single step count required for weight loss, though the 10,000-step target is commonly cited. Research indicates that taking between 4,000 and 10,000 steps per day can provide health benefits.
author: Medical Xpress

title: One-third of global food lost or wasted as policy focuses on production
content: Globally, approximately one-third of food produced for human consumption is estimated to be lost or wasted. While agricultural policy in the Global South has primarily focused on increasing production to address climate change and resource constraints, the issue of postharvest losses remains a significant challenge.
summary: Globally, about one-third of food produced for human consumption is estimated to be lost or wasted. Policy responses in the Global South have focused on increasing production rather than addressing postharvest losses.
author: Phys.org

title: Exiled researchers thrive by contributing knowledge to new academic networks
content: Publishing scientific articles relies on more than just knowledge of academic writing conventions, as it also depends on access to networks that support the research and publication process. These academic networks provide opportunities for researchers to exchange knowledge, receive feedback, and develop collaborations that strengthen both their research and careers. For researchers in vulnerable situations, such connections are particularly crucial.
summary: Publishing scientific articles depends on access to networks that support research and career development. These connections are crucial for researchers in vulnerable situations who exchange knowledge and develop collaborations.
author: Phys.org

title: Warwick astronomers reveal white dwarf stars glow in green, pink, and purple
content: Astronomers at the University of Warwick have demonstrated that white dwarf stars can emit light in a variety of colors, a finding that includes the discovery of the first star known to appear green to the human eye. This research reveals that these stellar remnants are not limited to a single hue but can glow in shades of green, pink, and purple.
summary: University of Warwick astronomers have shown that white dwarf stars can glow in a range of colors. This research includes the discovery of the first star ever found that would appear green to the human eye.
author: Phys.org

title: Fair climate transitions need more than financial support, evidence review suggests
content:
A recent evidence review indicates that fair climate transitions require measures beyond financial support. The transition to a low-carbon economy is not expected to affect all individuals and locations equally. While the overall benefits of the shift may exceed its costs, the process carries significant risks for specific groups.

Workers may face job losses, and households could encounter higher prices. Additionally, communities that depend on carbon-intensive industries may experience lasting economic and social disruption.
summary: The transition to a low‑carbon economy will affect people and places unevenly. Workers may lose jobs, households may face higher prices, and communities dependent on carbon‑intensive industries may experience lasting economic and social disruption, though overall benefits may outweigh costs.
author: Phys.org

title: Carrefour's Hopla AI shopping assistant raises trust vs human advice debate
content:
A shopper with a 20‑euro budget and a gluten‑intolerant guest may ask a shop assistant for advice or consult Hopla, the AI‑powered shopping assistant launched by French supermarket chain Carrefour.

Hopla provides meal suggestions that fit the budget and dietary restrictions.

This everyday choice raises a broader question: when faced with a recommendation, who do we trust more—a human being or an AI?
summary: Hopla, an AI‑powered shopping assistant, has been launched by French supermarket chain Carrefour. The service prompts a question of whether consumers will trust AI recommendations over human shop‑assistant advice when facing choices such as budgeting a 20‑euro dinner for a gluten‑intolerant guest.
author: Phys.org

title: Nepal flash flood triggered by rock and ice avalanche
content: A recent flash flood in Nepal was caused by an avalanche of rock and ice, the country’s disaster authority reported on Wednesday. The event is said to echo a similar mountain collapse that released a tsunami‑like wall of water in August.
summary: An avalanche of rock and ice triggered a recent flash flood in Nepal, according to the disaster authority. The event echoes a mountain collapse that unleashed a tsunami‑like wall of water in August.
author: Phys.org

title: Portsmouth study finds eco‑concerned tourists often won’t pay more for greener trips
content: Tourists who prioritize sustainability are not always willing to pay more for greener travel, a new study from the University of Portsmouth has found. The research indicates that concern for climate change does not automatically translate into higher spending on environmentally friendly holiday options.
summary: Tourists who care deeply about sustainability are not necessarily willing to pay extra to reduce the environmental impact of their vacations. The finding comes from new research conducted by the University of Portsmouth.
author: Phys.org

title: Social Service Agencies Must Implement Safeguards for AI Use
content: A University of Iowa researcher and former social worker warns that social service agencies require new safeguards as they increasingly adopt artificial intelligence to manage cases of child abuse, intimate partner violence, and elder abuse. The expert argues that without proper protections, AI systems risk introducing bias against vulnerable and disadvantaged populations.
summary: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used by social service agencies to handle cases involving child abuse, intimate partner violence, and elder abuse. A University of Iowa researcher and former social worker says agencies need safeguards to prevent bias against vulnerable or disadvantaged populations.
author: Phys.org

title: Nepal seeks to unite India and China against climate threats in the Himalayas
content:
India and China aren’t friends – but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats

In a bid to address a shared climate challenge, Nepal seeks to bring India and China together. The focus is on confronting a climate threat that affects the Himalayan region. The initiative aims to foster cooperation between the two regional giants in order to tackle the environmental issue.
summary: Nepal wants to unite India and China against a shared climate threat in the Himalayas. India and China aren't friends.
author: BBC Science

title: Sgiath, sea squirt‑hunting dog, honoured as animal of the year
content:
Sgiath, a dog trained to hunt the invasive sea squirt, has been recognised as the animal of the year. The canine is believed to be the first in the United Kingdom to specialise in locating this marine pest.

Sgiath has been trained to sniff out the sea squirt, a marine organism that poses a threat to local ecosystems. Its work in detecting the pest has earned it the honour of being named animal of the year.
summary: Sgiath is thought to be the UK's first sea squirt‑hunting dog. It has been trained to sniff out the marine pest.
author: BBC Science

content:
New open‑source model discussed on Hacker News

A post titled “A new model for open source: closed to pull requests, open to remix” was shared on Hacker News. The article proposes a shift in how open‑source projects handle contributions, suggesting that traditional pull‑request workflows be replaced with a remix‑centric approach.

content:
LFM2.5-24B-A2B: Built for fast on-device agents

title: Gudea uses AI to track and prevent social media crises before they erupt
content:
Gudea leverages AI to help organizations prevent social media crises before they erupt.  

Every day, conversations unfold across social media and websites worldwide. A seemingly insignificant post—whether it involves AI‑generated misinformation, hate speech, or a damaging rumor—can quickly snowball into a larger public controversy.  

Gudea, a company that tracks how stories and rumors spread online, describes itself as the “storm tracker for the internet.”
summary: Gudea tracks how stories and rumors spread online using AI. The company calls itself the “storm tracker for the internet” and helps organizations prevent social media crises before they erupt.
author: TechCrunch

title: Flock CEO Garrett Langley defends surveillance tech at TechCrunch Disrupt
content:
Flock CEO defends surveillance technology amid national backlash: “We shouldn’t pause progress”

At TechCrunch Disrupt, Garrett Langley, CEO of Flock, defended his company’s surveillance technology. He argued that the benefits for crime‑fighting outweigh the risks of abuse, even as privacy concerns grow.

Langley’s remarks came amid a national backlash over the use of surveillance tools. He maintained that progress should not be halted.
summary: Garrett Langley, CEO of Flock, defended his company's surveillance technology at TechCrunch Disrupt, saying “We shouldn’t pause progress.” He argued that its crime‑fighting benefits outweigh the risks of abuse despite growing privacy concerns and national backlash.
author: TechCrunch

title: Ricursive Intelligence bets on AI-designed chips to address compute crisis
content:
Ricursive Intelligence, a startup founded by a team of engineers, is betting on AI‑designed chips as a way to address the compute crisis. The company’s founders said the firm is creating artificial‑intelligence software that can generate chip designs.

According to the founders, the AI learns from each design iteration and uses that knowledge to improve subsequent versions, with the aim of automating and accelerating the chip‑design process.
summary: Ricursive Intelligence is betting on AI-designed chips to help solve the compute crisis. Its founders said the startup is developing AI that designs chips, learns from each iteration, and improves subsequent designs to automate and accelerate chip design.
author: TechCrunch

title: Lula’s party to file OAS complaint against Meta over alleged election interference
content:
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s party announced it will lodge a complaint against Meta with the Organization of American States, alleging the tech company interfered in the upcoming election. The party’s campaign said the filing will be made on Wednesday.

The complaint asserts that Meta restricted Lula’s online content in the weeks leading up to the presidential runoff scheduled for October 25, in which he faces Senator Flavio Bolsonaro. Meta has responded by denying the allegations.
summary: Lula’s party said it will file a complaint against Meta with the Organisation of American States, alleging the company restricted the president’s online content ahead of the October 25 runoff. Meta has denied the allegations.
author: France 24

title: US destroys Iran-affiliated dhow in Gulf of Oman, says it was conducting surveillance
content:
The United States said it destroyed a dhow that it suspected was being used for Iranian command and control operations.  

According to the U.S. statement, the Iran‑affiliated boat was located in the Gulf of Oman and was accused of conducting surveillance before being destroyed.
summary: The US says it destroyed an Iran-affiliated boat in the Gulf of Oman. The US accused the vessel of conducting surveillance.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran vows to fight until US yields as ships sink in Hormuz
content: Iran has said it does not seek an endless war but will continue fighting until the United States accepts its demands, amid reports of ships sinking in the Strait of Hormuz. The statement underscores Tehran’s commitment to maintain pressure while denying any intention for a prolonged conflict.
summary: Iran says it does not seek an endless war. Iran vows to fight until the US accepts its demands as ships sink in Hormuz.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Mexican court closes case against former migration chief over 2023 detention centre fire
content:
A Mexican court has closed the case against an official linked to a 2023 detention‑centre fire.  

Victims’ groups denounced the ruling, calling it “selective” justice that exonerates the former migration chief.  

The groups’ criticism highlights their disapproval of the court’s decision.
summary: A Mexican court has closed the case against the former migration chief related to the 2023 detention centre fire. Victims' groups denounced the ruling as selective justice that exonerates the official.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Costa Rica opens mega‑prison under President Laura Fernandez's tough‑on‑crime model
content:
Costa Rica inaugurated a new mega‑prison, a development the government says aligns with a regional shift toward stricter crime policies.  

President Laura Fernandez described the facility as part of the “tough‑on‑crime model” her administration has adopted, a model that the title links to the approach promoted by Bukele and embraced across Latin America.
summary: Costa Rica has opened a mega‑prison, according to President Laura Fernandez. She said the prison is part of the tough‑on‑crime model embraced by her government.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ship catches fire in Romanian waters, authorities probe possible drone involvement
content:
A ship caught fire in Romania’s waters, an incident that occurs amid a series of rising attacks in the Black Sea.  

Romanian authorities have opened an investigation into the blaze and are examining the possibility that drones were involved in the latest event.  

The probe remains ongoing as officials seek to determine the cause of the fire.
summary: A ship caught fire in Romania's waters. Authorities are investigating whether drones may have been involved in the latest incident.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Istanbul shut down by heaviest rainfall since 1985, flash floods hit city
content:
Istanbul was plunged into chaos and effectively shut down after experiencing the heaviest rainfall since 1985, according to reports.  

Torrential rain triggered flash floods across the city, overwhelming streets and infrastructure. The severe weather has left Istanbul grappling with widespread disruption.
summary: Istanbul was shut down by the heaviest rainfall since 1985. Torrential rain triggered flash floods across Istanbul.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Jackson and Barkley help Aston Villa beat Fenerbahce in record win
content:
Aston Villa secured their first home victory of the season and their biggest win in European competition history, defeating Fenerbahce with a dominant performance. The match marked a significant return for Mason Greenwood, who played his first game in England since January 2022, and saw the club celebrate a rediscovered attacking prowess despite the absence of the demolished North Stand.

Johan Manzambi opened the scoring on his 21st birthday and first Champions League appearance, setting the tone for Villa’s offensive display. Nicolas Jackson subsequently extended the lead with two goals before half-time, effectively putting the game beyond Fenerbahce’s reach. The home crowd at the Holte End responded with loud applause for the Villa players, while Greenwood received boos for every touch.
summary: Aston Villa secured their first home victory of the season and their biggest win in European competition against Fenerbahce. Nicolas Jackson scored two goals before half-time, while Johan Manzambi opened the scoring on his Champions League debut.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Doué and Dembélé Inspire PSG Win at Manchester City
content:
Pep Guardiola returned to the Etihad Stadium for the first time since his departure at the end of last season, attending a match where Paris Saint-Germain secured a victory over Manchester City. The former manager was seen wearing a flat cap in the stands, seated behind City chairman Khaldoon al-Mubarak and chief executive Ferran “Not” Soriano.

The match featured standout performances from Paris Saint-Germain players Ousmane Dembélé and Bradley Barcola, whose quickfire contributions inspired the team to a thrilling win.
summary: PSG secured a thrilling victory at Manchester City, driven by performances from Doué and Dembélé. Pep Guardiola returned to the Etihad Stadium for the first time since his departure at the end of last season.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Bradley Barcola hat-trick leads Liverpool to 6-3 Champions League win over LASK
content:
Liverpool secured a 6-3 victory over LASK in Austria, with Bradley Barcola delivering a hat‑trick to lead the Reds to the win. The match added a second consecutive triumph for Liverpool in the league phase of this season’s Champions League.

The result gives Liverpool two wins from two in the group stage, keeping them in strong position as the competition progresses.
summary: Bradley Barcola scored a hat-trick as Liverpool defeated LASK 6-3 in Austria. The win gave Liverpool two wins from two in the league phase of this season's Champions League.
author: BBC Sport

title: Martinez says United outburst came from anger and frustration
content: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has stated that his recent comments criticizing the club's hierarchy were made out of "anger and frustration." The player acknowledged that he spoke during an emotional moment, citing these intense feelings as the primary motivation behind his scathing remarks directed at the organization's leadership.
summary: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez stated that he spoke out of anger and frustration. He made these comments while addressing a scathing attack on the club's hierarchy.
author: BBC Sport

title: Bradley Barcola scores Champions League hat‑trick against Liverpool
content: Bradley Barcola delivered a decisive performance for Liverpool in their Champions League match against LASK, scoring a hat-trick. The France forward’s form had been a topic of discussion prior to the game, but his goals provided a definitive response to those pre-match questions.
summary: Bradley Barcola's form was the subject of pre‑match questions before Liverpool faced LASK. He answered by scoring a Champions League hat‑trick.

title: Guardiola Returns as Man City Defies PSG at Etihad
content: Phil McNulty describes Manchester City’s return to the Etihad Stadium as a display of defiance, despite facing a masterclass performance from Paris Saint-Germain. The match is characterized as a game of glorious chaos, highlighting the intensity of the contest between the two teams.
summary: Manchester City displayed defiance during their return to the Etihad Stadium. This occurred despite a masterclass performance by PSG.
author: BBC Sport

title: Voting Rights Group Threatens to Sue DOJ Over USB Voter List Demand
content: A voting rights group has warned the Department of Justice (DOJ) that it intends to file a lawsuit if the department does not retract a recent demand directed at California voting authorities. The order required these authorities to cross-reference their voter lists with data provided on a USB drive by the Trump administration within a 48-hour timeframe.
summary: A voting rights group warned the Department of Justice that it plans to sue if the department does not retract a demand made to California voting authorities. The demand ordered these authorities to cross-reference their voter lists with data on a USB drive provided by the Trump administration within 48 hours.
author: The Hill

title: Eight states sue OpenAI, alleging it misled users on chatbot safety
content:
Eight state attorneys general filed lawsuits against OpenAI on Wednesday, accusing the artificial intelligence firm of illegally misleading users regarding the safety of its ChatGPT product. The coalition alleges that OpenAI continued developing its AI products despite knowing that safety guardrails were required.

The group of state leaders, described as bipartisan, claims that OpenAI pushed forward with development while failing to adequately address safety concerns.
summary: A bipartisan group of eight state attorneys general sued OpenAI, accusing the company of illegally misleading users regarding the safety of its chatbot. The states allege that OpenAI pushed forward with AI product development despite knowing its products require safety guardrails.
author: The Hill

title: Harris tells Keke Palmer she is undecided on 2028 presidential run
content:
Former Vice President Kamala Harris told actor Keke Palmer that she has not yet decided whether to run for president in 2028. Harris made the comments during a lengthy interview on Palmer’s podcast, “Baby, This is Keke Palmer,” amid growing speculation about a potential third campaign for the Democrat.

The conversation covered several topics, including the Trump administration and the upcoming midterm elections. Harris also discussed her time serving as vice president during the interview.
summary: Former Vice President Kamala Harris told actor Keke Palmer that she has not yet decided on a presidential run in 2028. Harris made these remarks during an interview on Palmer's podcast, "Baby, This is Keke Palmer."
author: The Hill

title: Trump rallies in Montana for Aaron Flint in 1st District race
content: President Trump campaigned in Montana on Wednesday evening to support Republican candidate Aaron Flint, who is challenging Democrat Sam Forstag for the state’s 1st Congressional District. The race aims to replace retiring Representative Ryan Zinke (R-Mont.) as Republicans seek to maintain their majorities in both chambers of Congress.
summary: President Trump is campaigning in Montana to support Republican Aaron Flint, who is running against Democrat Sam Forstag. The race is for the 1st Congressional District seat previously held by retiring Rep. Ryan Zinke.
author: The Hill

title: Sally Rooney says Palestine Action support blocks UK book sales
content:
Irish novelist Sally Rooney has stated that her support for Palestine Action, an organization banned by the British government, has resulted in her books being blocked from sale in the United Kingdom. Rooney, known for her works "Normal People" and "Intermezzo," disclosed this information in an interview with The Guardian on Wednesday.

The author explained that the sales restriction followed the British government’s decision to proscribe the protest group as a terrorist organization.
summary: Irish novelist Sally Rooney stated that her support for the banned group Palestine Action prevents her from selling books in the United Kingdom. She told The Guardian that the British government proscribed the protest group as a terrorist organization.
author: The Hill

title: Ukraine faces crisis as satellite restrictions and questions over Trump's role emerge
content: The war in Ukraine and the question of the American role have entered a new period of chaos and crisis, marked by a blizzard of developments on Wednesday. title: CoScreen founders launch Petal, a free open-source pair programming tool
content:
Jason Thomas, a co-founder of CoScreen, announced the release of Petal, a free and open-source pair programming tool developed by four members of the original CoScreen team. This launch follows Datadog’s decision to sunset the CoScreen service on July 31st. The team stated that they built Petal to break the recurring industry pattern where standalone screen-sharing tools are acquired by larger platforms and subsequently shut down, citing the 2017 discontinuation of ScreenHero and the 2025 shutdown of Around as examples.

Petal allows shared windows to appear as real, movable, and resizable windows on a user’s desktop rather than tiles in a grid. Multiple participants can share simultaneously, each with a labeled cursor, and users can click into any shared window to type or scroll. The platform supports persistent rooms, allowing users to join specific sessions like "eng-sync" without sharing links. Currently available on macOS and Windows, with a web app and Linux support planned, the tool uses LiveKit for media transmission and can be self-hosted via Docker or used with a zero-config hosted instance.

The developers noted that the initial version of Petal was built in under eight weeks, significantly faster than the nearly six years required to build CoScreen, with assistance from frontier models named Fable and Astra. Thomas, along with team members Till, Darren, and Max, stated that the project is not monetized and is designed to allow the community to self-host or fork the software, preventing it from being sunset by corporate decisions.
summary: Jason Thomas and three former CoScreen team members released Petal, a free and open-source collaborative screen sharing tool, after Datadog sunset the CoScreen service. Petal allows users to share real desktop windows with multiple participants and supports self-hosting to prevent future shutdowns.
